title: Add optional schematic pin-label font size
description: Adds an optional display_pin_label_font_size field to schematic_port, allowing for per-port font size adjustments for pin labels without affecting the entire symbol.
body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `display_pin_label_font_size` field to `schematic_port`.

The field accepts:

- a positive finite number in schematic millimeters
- `"default"`
- `"sm"`

When omitted, existing schematic ports remain unchanged.

## Why

This carries the per-port `schPinLabelFontSize` value introduced in tscircuit/props#810 through Circuit JSON. It allows downstream renderers to adjust a crowded pin label without scaling the whole symbol or changing unrelated ports.

This PR only defines the Circuit JSON contract. Core and circuit-to-svg support will be added in separate follow-up PRs.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 307 passed
- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run lint:zod`
- `bun run check-snake-case`
- changed files pass Biome formatting

title: feat: add castellated holes to board outlines
description: Proposes an additive way to describe castellated holes directly in a board  outline.
body:
## Summary

Proposes an additive way to describe castellated holes directly in a `<board />` outline:

```tsx
<board
  outline={[
    { x: "-5mm", y: "-5mm" },
    {
      x: "-5mm",
      y: 0,
      isCastellatedHole: true,
      holeDiameter: "0.8mm",
      padDiameter: "1.2mm",
      connectsTo: "net.GND",
    },
    { x: "-5mm", y: "5mm" },
    { x: "5mm", y: "5mm" },
    { x: "5mm", y: "-5mm" },
  ]}
/>
```

Each flagged point is both an ordinary outline vertex and the center of the castellated hole. Existing `Point[]` outlines remain valid without migration.

## API decisions

- `isCastellatedHole` marks the outline point; its related geometry and connectivity props are flat on the same object.
- `holeDiameter` and `padDiameter` are required when `isCastellatedHole` is true, making the drill and copper dimensions explicit without manufacturing-sensitive defaults.
- `connectsTo` is optional and accepts one or more connection targets, also matching `<platedhole />`.
- Distance strings are normalized to millimeters by the existing distance parser.
- The type and schema are exported as `BoardOutlinePoint` and `boardOutlinePoint` for downstream consumers.

This PR is intentionally the props/API layer. Follow-up work in `circuit-json` and `core` will need to preserve the annotations in `pcb_board` output and materialize the fabrication/rendering behavior.

Related to tscircuit/tscircuit#3297.

## Testing

- `bun test`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run check-circular-deps`
- `bun run format:check`
- required generated documentation scripts

title: fix: synchronize fanout exits across named nets
description: Fixes synchronization of fanout exits across named nets to ensure proper routing connections and continuity assertions in PCB designs.
body: ## Summary - matches local fanout and global routing connections by their shared breakout-point identity when named-net expansion gives them different source trace IDs - updates each global routing endpoint to the compacted fanout exit - centralizes SRJ point matching with documented board-world coordinates, stable point identity, and position-plus-layer fallback semantics - adds physical copper-continuity assertions at every handoff - updates the same 4x4 BGA PCB SVG so R1-R3 visibly route all the way to U1 The otherwise-unconnected resistor pins are compact visual endpoints for this routing reproduction, not a functional pull-up network. ## SVG before and after - base snapshot in #3445: the three resistor stubs and three BGA fanout traces end at different coordinates - fixed snapshot in this PR: each resistor route reaches the corresponding fanout exit; the BGA itself and component placement stay unchanged ## Stack - base repro: #3445 - this PR contains only the handoff fix, continuity assertions, shared SRJ comparison utility, and resulting SVG change ## Validation - focused visual repro: 1 passed with 9 assertions - SRJ endpoint comparison contract: 1 passed with 6 assertions - paired exit-target layer test: 1 passed - breakout tests: 22 passed, 2 skipped - memory-capped bun run build: passed, including declaration generation

title: test: reproduce disconnected fanout net handoff
description: Reproduces a bug where disconnected fanout net handoff occurs during autorouting, with a test case to demonstrate the issue.
body:
## Summary

- adds a minimal, visually recognizable 4x4 BGA named U1
- places three external resistors R1-R3 just outside the fanout region
- connects three BGA balls to those resistor endpoints through named nets
- records the disconnected handoff produced when fanout compaction moves the local exits but the global traces retain the original breakout coordinates

The otherwise-unconnected resistor pins keep this routing reproduction visually small. They are fixture endpoints, not a functional pull-up network.

## Reading the SVG

The dashed inner rectangle is the BGA fanout phase, and its left edge sits between U1 and the resistors. In the buggy snapshot, three traces leave U1 and terminate on that boundary. The short traces from R1, R2, and R3 terminate at three stale coordinates inside the region, so none touches its matching BGA trace. The note at the top states the expected result.

## Stack status

This draft intentionally records the pre-fix output and should not merge by itself. The fix is stacked on this branch as #3446.

## Test

- bun test tests/repros/repro-breakout-fanout-net-handoff-gap.test.tsx

title: Support compact passive schSize variants
description: Maps schSize variants sm and xs to compact passive symbols for resistors and capacitors, preserving existing styles and behaviors.
body:
## Summary

- map `schSize="sm"` and `schSize="xs"` to the premade compact passive symbols released in [`schematic-symbols@0.0.242`](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-symbols/pull/459)
- preserve the selected resistor style: the default IEC box uses `boxresistor_sm` / `boxresistor_xs`, while `symbolName="resistor"` uses the compact US zigzag family
- use `capacitor_sm` / `capacitor_xs` for non-polar capacitors while leaving polarized capacitors unchanged
- keep orientation suffixing centralized and fall back to the original symbol base when compact symbols are unavailable through an older wildcard peer dependency

## Behavior

| JSX | Selected symbol base |
| --- | --- |
| `<resistor schSize="sm" />` | `boxresistor_sm` |
| `<resistor schSize="xs" />` | `boxresistor_xs` |
| `<resistor symbolName="resistor" schSize="sm" />` | `resistor_sm` |
| `<resistor symbolName="resistor" schSize="xs" />` | `resistor_xs` |
| `<capacitor schSize="sm" />` | `capacitor_sm` |
| `<capacitor schSize="xs" />` | `capacitor_xs` |

`@tscircuit/props` already accepts `xs` and `sm` for resistor and capacitor `schSize`, so no props release is required. `default`, `md`, numeric distances, custom symbol names, and compact polarized capacitors retain their existing behavior in this change.

## Validation

- `bun test`: 1,452 passed, 40 skipped, 0 failed; 58 snapshots and 8,396 assertions
- focused passive-size test: 1 passed, 16 assertions
- compact-symbol regression set: 6 passed, 32 assertions
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run smoke-test:dist`
- `bunx biome format .`
- `git diff --check`

## Snapshot review

Reviewed the actual Core schematic render on one shared-scale canvas, covering default / sm / xs IEC resistors and capacitors, compact US zigzag resistors, rotated compact variants, and the polarized fallback. The 0.50-unit sm and 0.35-unit xs pin spans are visibly distinct, the bodies and plates remain legible, and REF / value labels do not clip or collide.

Related to #3106 and #3108. This PR intentionally does not close them because `md`, numeric-distance sizing, and the obsolete `small` spelling are outside its scope.

## Summary

- strengthen the nRF52810 repro against the GND/VBAT accidental contact and via-to-X1-pad clearance regression

## Same-machine Pipeline 7 benchmark

The [same-machine benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2230#issuecomment-5419319871) ran 85 dataset01 scenarios:

- completion: 100% → 100%
- relaxed DRC pass rate: 100% → 100%
- DRC issues: 0 → 0
- timeouts: 0 → 0
- average vias: 37.96 → 37.96
- outcomes: 0 improved, 0 regressed
- timing changes ranged from -5.4% to +4.7%; P95 was +1.9%

This indicates no material performance regression. Because the autorouter PR had already merged, the run compared release-main against the retained PR head; it verifies published/head parity rather than a clean pre-merge-parent comparison.

## DRC and snapshot review

- the newly exposed GND/VBAT trace contact is absent
- the X1-adjacent via/pad clearance error is absent, with zero via-clearance errors in the repro
- only the affected GND route and its two layer-transition vias changed; component, pad, silkscreen, board, and all other route geometry are unchanged
- the repro still has two known pre-existing routing DRCs (oscillator trace contact and P0_25/GND clearance), so this PR does not claim the fixture is fully DRC-clean

title: Render schematic pin-label font size overrides
description: Uses the optional numeric schematic_port.display_pin_label_font_size value when rendering schematic pin labels, allowing for precise font size adjustments for crowded imported symbols without altering the symbol or adding collision heuristics.
body:
## Summary

Uses the optional numeric `schematic_port.display_pin_label_font_size` value when rendering schematic pin labels.

The existing renderer defaults remain unchanged when the field is omitted:

- normal pin labels continue to use `0.15mm`
- negated and inversion-circle labels continue to use `0.12mm`
- an explicit numeric value overrides either default

## Why

This completes the renderer layer for per-port pin-label sizing. It lets producers provide a precise font size for crowded imported symbols without scaling the symbol or adding renderer-side collision heuristics.

Circuit JSON support was added in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/723.
The Core integration is https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3430.

## Scope

The production change only passes the validated Circuit JSON value to the existing schematic font-size helper. It does not add label measurement, collision detection, part-specific values, or new rotation logic.

title: fix: detect via copper overlapping pad corners
description: Fixes detection of via copper overlapping pad corners to ensure accurate placement error reporting.
body:
## Stacked PR

This fix is stacked on reproduction PR #242 and addresses #241. Its base is repro/issue-241-via-pad-corner-overlap, not main. Do not merge it independently of the reproduction boundary.

PR #242 uses Bun test.failing semantics so the known-bug assertion executes as an expected failure without making CI red. This PR explicitly converts that qualifier back to ordinary test(...) because the fix satisfies the assertion.

## Root cause and fix

checkViasInPads queried the spatial index at only the via center and then tested only whether that point was inside a pad. A via whose center was outside a rectangular pad could therefore be skipped even when its copper radius crossed an edge or corner.

The check now queries with the full via copper bounds and uses the existing shape-aware getPadToPadGap geometry. A gap at or below zero is contact/overlap; a positive gap remains clear. Existing board-level via-in-pad allowance and shared-layer filtering are unchanged.

The placement message now describes copper overlap instead of claiming the via center is inside the pad.

## Visual acceptance

The #242 snapshot changes from placement via/pad overlap errors: 0 to 1 and adds the rendered error text naming the via coordinates and R1.pin1.

## Verification

- Focused tests — 12 passed, 0 failed
- bun test — 187 passed, 0 failed
- bun run build — passed, including declaration generation
- Targeted Biome formatting and git diff --check — passed

Repository-wide bun run format:check still stops on the pre-existing 1 MiB Biome size limit for three unchanged JSON fixtures; all changed source and test files pass formatting.

This is the first PR in a two-PR stack for #241. It intentionally adds no geometry fix.

The SVG snapshot labels the conflicting copper and records that placement currently reports zero via/pad overlap errors.

title: Add compact passive symbol variants
description: Add compact passive symbol variants including small and extra-small box resistors, US resistors, and capacitors with various orientations and dimensions.
body:
## Summary

- add `sm` and `xs` box resistor, US resistor, and capacitor bases, each exported in right, left, up, and down orientations
- use common terminal spans of `0.50` for `sm` and `0.35` for `xs`
- preserve recognizable bodies and capacitor plates while removing proportionally more lead length
- reduce the US resistor zigzag from 8 geometry vertices in `sm` to 6 in `xs`, while preserving its `0.19` peak-to-peak height
- preserve capacitor `pos`/`neg` aliases, readable REF/VAL annotations, generated exports, and snapshots

## Geometry rationale

These are intentionally not uniform scales of the existing symbols. KiCad's [small US resistor](https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-symbols/-/blob/v9/Device.kicad_sym?ref_type=heads#L145378) reduces zigzag turns while retaining tooth amplitude, and compact Altium passives similarly concentrate their recognizable geometry in the body/plates with short external leads. The `0.50` small span also follows the historical maintainer sizing guidance in #276; `0.35` is a proportional extra-small step selected through shared-scale visual review.

The resulting right-facing geometry is:

| family | `sm` | `xs` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| box resistor | `0.35 × 0.15` body, `0.075` stems | `0.28 × 0.13` body, `0.035` stems |
| US resistor | `0.32 × 0.19` body, `0.09` stems | `0.23 × 0.19` body, `0.06` stems |
| capacitor | `0.32` plate height, `0.12` gap, `0.19` stems | `0.28` plate height, `0.10` gap, `0.125` stems |

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bun test`
- `bun run snapshot:validate`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- visually reviewed all 24 snapshots plus shared-scale and all-orientation comparison grids

This PR adds the premade symbol bases and exports. Wiring component `schSize` selection to these bases remains a separate core integration.

title: fix: preserve default platform config maps
description: Fixes the issue where custom project configurations could erase built-in footprint resolvers and other default settings, ensuring that defaults are preserved unless explicitly overridden by the project.
body:
## Summary

- deep-merge project platform-map overrides with the CLI defaults
- preserve built-in footprint resolvers, file parsers, static loaders, autorouters, and SPICE engines unless the project overrides the same key
- add regression coverage for the build pipeline's normalized, SPICE-only project config

## Root cause

The build worker first combines platform configs with `mergePlatformConfigs`. That helper materializes absent nested maps as `{}`. `getPlatformConfigWithCliDefaults` then shallow-spread the normalized project config over the default config, so an empty `footprintLibraryMap` erased the built-in `kicad` and `jlcpcb` resolvers.

This meant a project that only configured a custom `spiceEngineMap` could no longer load KiCad footprints. It surfaced as `No footprint resolver is configured for library "kicad"` in [this TI release build](https://tscircuit.com/tscircuit/ti/releases/c426ce29-c854-41fe-be28-3a835b67b418).

The fix reuses the existing map-aware merge helper with defaults first and project config second, so project entries still take precedence.

Companion cleanup for the three stale identifiers exposed after restoring the resolvers: tscircuit/ti#139.

## Testing

- `bun test tests/shared/get-platform-config-with-cli-defaults.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- related build-concurrency and static-file-loader tests

The regression first passes a SPICE-only config through `mergePlatformConfigs`, confirms the empty maps produced by that normalization step, and then verifies all CLI defaults survive.

title: fix: transpile explicit TypeScript extension imports
description: Preserves explicit .ts.tsx imports during library transpilation by enabling TypeScript 5.7 relative-extension rewriting and retaining fallback for older TypeScript versions.
body:
## Summary

- preserve explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` imports during library transpilation by enabling TypeScript 5.7+ relative-extension rewriting
- retain the existing fallback for older TypeScript versions
- add a regression test covering a user tsconfig with `allowImportingTsExtensions`

## Cause

The transpiler unconditionally overrode `allowImportingTsExtensions` to `false` because plain TypeScript emit cannot use it. Projects such as `tscircuit/ti` intentionally import `.tsx` files and therefore produced TS5097 for every import during both ESM and CJS bundling. TypeScript 5.7 introduced `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`, which makes this combination emit-safe.

Reproduction: https://tscircuit.com/tscircuit/ti/releases/1a2d8fe2-3a34-468a-9557-70d7102d837b

## Validation

- `bun test tests/cli/transpile/transpile.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/cli/build/build-transpile.test.ts`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- `bun ../cli/cli/main.ts build --ci --concurrency 4` against tscircuit/ti PR #120: 118/118 circuits passed, followed by ESM, CJS, and declaration generation without TS5097
- the generated ESM, CJS, and declaration artifacts for that PR are byte-identical before and after this change

## Summary

- pin high-density-repair03 PR #82 so the connectivity map is authoritative when exact DRC resolves electrical nets
- add the complete nRF52810 Pipeline7 fixture plus the historical bad exact-geometry candidate
- assert that the fixed exact stage keeps the two real inherited issues, introduces neither the GND/VBAT contact nor the X1 via-pad violation, and emits no new post-power DRC identities
- add a three-panel reviewer-visible SVG: safe exact input, historical bad candidate, fixed exact output
- refresh only three existing route snapshots whose output actually changes under the fix

## Root cause

Pipeline7 exact DRC resolved a routed trace to a generated connectivity-net id but could resolve a connected raw PCB port to a point-pair alias. The same electrical net then compared unequal, inflating the exact DRC inventory and steering repair toward a lower-count candidate that introduced two real violations. The newer connectivity-monotone power expander stopped incidentally repairing that unsafe candidate, which exposed the defect in the nRF52810 snapshot.

This does not add an output-blocking gate. The fix corrects the DRC input classification before candidate selection.

## Snapshot review

- bugreport99: focused visual explicitly marks the historical GND/VBAT contact and X1 via-pad hotspot between safe input and fixed output
- bugreport44: one via is placed on the shorter valid candidate; the same single pre-existing via-pad error remains
- bugreport89 and bugreport92: identical SRJs remain reference-DRC-clean, with 37 traces and 18 vias; routed length changes by only 0.12 percent
- six other local Darwin snapshot mismatches were byte-identical between the old and fixed dependency and were intentionally left out of this PR

## Validation

- focused nRF and neighboring Pipeline7 DRC suite: 7 pass, 46 assertions
- reviewed snapshot set: 4 pass, 15 assertions
- bunx tsc --noEmit
- bun run build
- bun run format:check
- git diff --check
- high-density-repair03: 83 pass, 0 fail
- capacity full run before selective snapshot refresh: 569 pass, 60 skip; nine visual mismatches, with three attributable and refreshed here and six proven unrelated by old/fixed byte comparison

## Summary

- try both sides of routed traces and terminal stubs before falling back to anchored labels
- derive inline placements for opted-in multi-pin nets from solved trace-connected components
- atomically replace short routed components only when every pin in the component remains represented
- treat `available-net-orientation-*` traces as generated anchored-label connectors, not routed circuitry, so converted endpoints receive real inline terminal stubs

- exercise the merged DRV8305 motor-driver repro with rats-net rendering hidden

title: Fix local GND labels for independent capacitor branches
description: Fixes the routing of local GND labels for independent capacitor branches to prevent unintended connections between them, ensuring proper electrical isolation and labeling in the schematic.
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to [#934](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/pull/934). That PR is now merged, so this PR targets `main`.

- keep the shared C1/C2/VSS rail, with its GND symbol on the outer C1 column
- terminate C3 and C4 locally with GND symbols instead of routing return wires between the capacitors
- preserve the electrical GND net, explicit connections, component placement, and level capacitor rails
- prevent the long-distance routing pass from reconnecting the intentionally separated branches

## Routing scope and safety

The local-ground preference applies to independent, downward-facing two-pin branches when the same ground net contains an explicitly wired, level parallel-load rail. Nearby pins within a 1 mm vertical offset, directly wired branches, and other ground topologies retain their existing behavior. There are no component-name or circuit-specific checks.

After rail alignment, the shared GND label can move to the outer load column only if its body is clear of components, text, traces, and other labels. Port-only labels and labels on unrelated islands stay attached to their own branches.

## Actual TI reference

![TI basic application schematic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/17cf5ac3d6ea1c4c58258ef3191c013d09ae4d0a/lib/subcircuits/Microcontroller_MSPM0L1306.reference.png)

Source circuit: [tscircuit/ti#119](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/pull/119).

## Before

The capacitor rails are aligned, but the ground return still connects the decoupling rail to C3 and C4.

![Before: interconnected ground returns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/8249d0865af57467c19b5031c645690b2cd5afb2/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-mspm0l1306-capacitor-symmetry.snap.svg)

## Generated snapshot after the fix

The shared decoupling rail, VCORE capacitor, and reset capacitor now have local GND terminations.

![After: local capacitor grounds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/1e83eff833583913ad7216d052d365f5187a0459/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-mspm0l1306-capacitor-symmetry.snap.svg)

The existing full-circuit repro now asserts separate C3/C4 ground terminations, the outer rail label, unchanged ground connectivity, and level VDD/VSS rails. One other board snapshot also changes: a long ground return is replaced by two local labels; its before/after rendering was reviewed.

## Validation

title: Fix symmetric routing for parallel capacitor rails
description: Fixes routing symmetry for parallel capacitor rails by aligning downward-facing and upward-facing rails, reusing the outer capacitor column for return branches, and ensuring no additional cross-net intersections are introduced.
body:
## Stack

Stacked on [#933](https://github.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/pull/933), which adds the unmodified circuit input and baseline snapshot. Merge the repro first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

## Summary

- align downward-facing parallel-load rails as well as upward-facing rails
- reuse the outer capacitor column for the return branch instead of introducing a third column between C1 and C2
- level the rails before aligning return branches, preserving component positions, endpoint pins, and net connectivity
- retain obstacle and label checks; reject reroutes that introduce additional cross-net intersections, including crossings at bends or against single-segment traces
- try a shorter return-pin escape when the original escape would cross another net, while retaining a minimum pin stem

For the MSPM0L1306 circuit, the C1/C2 lower rail now runs straight to VSS at y=0.65, and the return continues down the C1 column. Both capacitor columns now have matching top and bottom rail junctions.

description: Aligns same-net rail chains while preserving fixed outward net-label anchors, ensuring that the alignment does not affect the readability or positioning of labels.
body:
## Summary

- Preserve fixed outward net-label anchors while aligning same-net rail chains through shared pins.
- Align complete capacitor chains to the uniquely labeled terminal rail, including all three branches in the July 30 regression.
- Generate the three-pin GND connector from the adjacent rail bend without changing longer multi-pin rail ordering.
- Add exact regressions for the top capacitor rail, unchanged C26 rail, three-pin GND connector, and remote Type-C GND label.

## Implementation

- Same-net alignment remains contained in `TraceCleanupSolver/sameNetRailAlignment`.
- Existing nearest-endpoint rail groups retain their original behavior and ordering.
- Tied endpoint associations are considered only for local connections and only when a fixed label anchors the expanded group.
- Fixed labels may override readability scoring only for single-rail traces. Per-connection locality is retained unless the label is carried by an intentional multi-turn routed backbone.
- Connector selection stays in `AvailableNetOrientationSolver`; the nearest bend tie-break applies only when the outward row belongs to a trace directly adjacent to the label host.
- Repeated rail states terminate deterministically, preventing endpoint-component oscillation and maximum-pass parity changes.
- No post-processing was added to `Example28Solver` or `labelMovement.ts`.
- No bug-specific coordinates, component IDs, net names, generated-trace prefix checks, or duplicated path-intersection geometry are used.

## Blast-radius audit

- Regenerated the full suite and inspected every remaining snapshot structurally and visually.
- Reduced the snapshot diff from 18 files to 5.
- Restored `repro-type-c-vbus-led-ground-label`, `repro-bq25895-cross-net-trace-overlap`, `bug-report-20260707T141421Z`, `bug-report-20260728T144234Z`, `repro-tida010076-page02`, `board-1273-trace-overlap-cycle`, and `bug-report-20260721T221026Z` exactly to `main`.

description: Fixes DRC net canonicalization issues by treating injected connectivity map net IDs as authoritative, preventing misclassification of connected trace and pad copper as different nets.
body:
## Summary

- treat the injected connectivity map net id as authoritative before SRJ point-pair aliases
- prevent Pipeline7 exact DRC from classifying connected trace and pad copper as different nets
- add a focused regression and reviewer-visible SVG comparing the same-net exemption with a true foreign-net DRC

## Root cause

The DRC engine resolved a dynamic trace to a generated connectivity net id, but could resolve a connected raw PCB port to its point-pair connection alias. Those identifiers described the same electrical net but compared unequal, inflating the DRC inventory and steering exact-geometry repair toward an unsafe candidate.

## Summary

- add `ClockBuffer_LMK1C1104`, filling the `Clocks & timing` → `Clock buffers` category represented in `ti-sysblocks`
- add and export the LMK1C1104 TSSOP-8 chip model
- reproduce the functional drawing area of TI's LMK1C1104EVM Altium schematic with all 64 components, 160 ports, the input/power/output topology, Y0–Y7 validation fixtures, and the source's DNP population state
- expose `CLKIN`, `OE`, `VDD`, `GND`, and the four driven outputs `Y0`–`Y3` through `exposedNets`; use connected native `<netlabel>` elements for the public signal endpoints
- retain Y4–Y7 only as internal DNP validation-fixture nets because the four-output LMK1C1104 does not drive them
- preserve all 36 circuit-body engineering-note lines with `<schematictext>` while omitting their background frames; the Altium sheet border, TI title block/logo, parameter fields, and legal/footer boilerplate are intentionally omitted
- update generated schematic and routed PCB snapshots

`OE` is the public API alias for TI's `1G` pin/net label because tscircuit net selectors cannot begin with a digit. The chip symbol still identifies the physical pin as `1G`.

Consumers can instantiate the subcircuit and connect through the exposed parent nets, for example `net.CLKIN`, `net.OE`, and `net.Y0`–`net.Y3`.

## Reference and conversion

- `ti-sysblocks` lists LMK1C1104 under [Clocks & timing → Clock buffers](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti-sysblocks/blob/4812e9499380354f5864516b50be8b7445f8622d/lib/generated/machine-vision-camera.json#L2092-L2126)
- TI reference design: [LMK1C1104EVM](https://www.ti.com/tool/LMK1C1104EVM)
- native Altium source: [SNAR039.ZIP](https://www.ti.com/lit/zip/SNAR039)
- supporting schematic/BOM: [SNAU249](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/SNAU249)

`HSDC078A_Validation_Board_Schematic.SchDoc` was converted with `altium-to-circuit-json` v0.0.13 (`97e5b2e4bb9acba337af0de07d74287e5e089f2a`) using:

```sh
bun run scripts/convert-single-reference.ts HSDC078A_Validation_Board_Schematic.SchDoc schematic.circuit.json
```

The normalized conversion contains 917 Circuit JSON elements and validates cleanly. Altium stored 49 passive MPNs in `Comment` while hiding their electrical values in `Value`; normalization restored those resistor/capacitor values before validation.

Provenance hashes:

- `SNAR039.ZIP`: `2fd36888e5713ba79fe4f79e41332dc87eed296656d6cd5785cbf95bcabc4781`
- main `.SchDoc`: `787e4a3067ffd033d45af0b09c6bccdf704f1e3801d38eaa9f99ae3af644d761`
- normalized Circuit JSON: `4ed3e68e6e4558bf9fbf0a42ccd8b46ad63c5e0bc9d1ef2857f924933399a55c`

The Altium PCB document is an unsynchronized 16-pin LMK1C1108 validation layout. The schematic and BOM identify the actual LMK1C1104 as `PW0008A` TSSOP-8, so this implementation uses the correct 8-pin footprint and a newly routed PCB snapshot rather than claiming literal PCB reproduction.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bunx tsci build lib/subcircuits/ClockBuffer_LMK1C1104.circuit.tsx`
- `bunx tsci snapshot lib/subcircuits/ClockBuffer_LMK1C1104.circuit.tsx --test --concurrency 1`
- `git diff --check`
- nested-consumer audit of every exposed-net bridge
- root export/map smoke check
- Circuit JSON audit: 64 source/schematic/PCB components, 160 source/schematic/PCB ports, 114 source traces, 91 schematic traces, 106 PCB traces, 36 vias, 12 explicit nets, correct ground/power flags, and zero `*_error` records

The nested-consumer audit verifies parent connectivity for exactly `CLKIN`, `OE`, `VDD`, `GND`, and `Y0`–`Y3`, while Y4–Y7 remain scoped to their DNP fixtures.

The build succeeds. Its remaining placement warnings come from retaining TI's tightly packed validation-fixture geometry; supplier-footprint IoU and unnamed-trace messages are non-fatal.

## Related work

Open PR #112 contains a datasheet-derived LMK1C1104 example and a different package variant, but it does not add a reusable component under `lib/subcircuits`. This PR uses the TSSOP-8 package from the Altium EVM schematic/BOM.

body:
## Summary

- replace all 373 `AM62L32BOGHAANBR` pads' generic 0.30 mm land geometry with TI's AM62L-specific 10 mil (0.254 mm) NSMD land
- add the corresponding 1 mil (0.0254 mm) solder-mask margin, producing TI's 12 mil mask opening
- centralize the geometry in a shared constant and add a focused Circuit JSON regression test for pad count, geometry, identities, and endpoint positions

## Rationale

TI's generic MPBGB03 package drawing shows a 0.30 mm PCB land example and 0.25–0.35 mm component balls. For AM62L escape routing, however, [SPRADI2 Table 3-1](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/spradi2) gives a device-specific 10 mil land and 12 mil solder-mask opening. This change uses that exact recommendation: a 0.127 mm pad radius and 0.0254 mm solder-mask margin.

The downstream reproduction previously monkey-patched the package footprint to a 0.25616 mm diameter. That value was derived from the routing equation `0.5 mm pitch - 3 × 0.08128 mm`, not specified by TI, so it is intentionally not upstreamed. TI's documented 0.254 mm land is used instead. See also the [MPBGB03 package drawing](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/mpbgb03).

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 1 focused test, 373 pads, all at radius 0.127 mm and solder-mask margin 0.0254 mm; pin identities and endpoint positions preserved
- `bunx tsci build lib/chips/AM62L32BOGHAANBR.circuit.tsx` — passed; generated Circuit JSON contains exactly 373 pads with the expected geometry
- `bun run build` — all 117 package circuits built successfully (exit 0)
- linked downstream `ddr-byte1-only` build — all six autorouter phases completed without autorouter errors; U1 has the new 373-pad geometry and U2 is unchanged
- downstream netlist check, layer verification, and shorts check all passed; 11 source nets produced 33 PCB traces and 28 vias

The downstream DRC still reports the same two pre-existing via-to-trace clearance locations near DQ9 and DQ15 (0.006 mm and 0.021 mm versus a 0.05 mm minimum). Those diagnostics were already present with the old monkey patch; they are not shorts, and routing otherwise completes. After this package is released, consumers can remove the React footprint monkey patch and use the component normally.

description: Summary honor bus maxLengthSkew as a hard fanout constraint add straight45-degree meanders after the dense pad escape without changing endpoints or vias apply matching atomically to complete normal and grouped-beam route candidates reject impossible constraints instead of emitting a skew violation validate declared plan lengths, final bus skew, unsupported plane termination, and invalid inputs add synthetic and captured AM62L visual regressions  Why Core already forwards maxLengthSkew into fanout phases, but the solver previously dropped it. This adds a native fanout-aware matcher so the existing one-via escape topology and exact DRC checks remain authoritative. I evaluated tscircuitlength-matching-solver, but did not add it as a dependency: its current package is unpublished and its public API is differential-pairHD-route oriented rather than an atomic multi-member fanout-bus API.  Snapshots Captured AM62L SOC BYTE1 fanout, matched from 9.611899 mm to 8.499999 mm phase-local skew: !AM62L SOC length matching(https:github.comtscircuitfanout-solverblobfeatfanout-length-matchingtests__snapshots__am62l-soc-length-matching.snap.svg?raw1) Compact synthetic regression, matched from 1.112 mm to at most 0.25 mm: !Length-matched fanout(https:github.comtscircuitfanout-solverblobfeatfanout-length-matchingtests__snapshots__bus-length-matching.snap.svg?raw1)  Validation bun run typecheck Biome checks on all changed source, test, fixture, and documentation files focused AM62L, length-matching, winding, repair, and no-right-angle tests full suite: 104 pass; the sole failure is the pre-existing Dataset07 boundary-core SVG snapshot mismatch The captured AM62L regression uses the exact Core phase input, tunes two BYTE1 traces, preserves exactly one via on all 16 routed DQ traces, and passes both solver validation and an independent emitted-copper DRC audit. body:
## Summary

- honor bus `maxLengthSkew` as a hard fanout constraint
- add straight/45-degree meanders after the dense pad escape without changing endpoints or vias
- apply matching atomically to complete normal and grouped-beam route candidates
- reject impossible constraints instead of emitting a skew violation
- validate declared plan lengths, final bus skew, unsupported plane termination, and invalid inputs
- add synthetic and captured AM62L visual regressions

## Why

Core already forwards `maxLengthSkew` into fanout phases, but the solver previously dropped it. This adds a native fanout-aware matcher so the existing one-via escape topology and exact DRC checks remain authoritative.

I evaluated `@tscircuit/length-matching-solver`, but did not add it as a dependency: its current package is unpublished and its public API is differential-pair/HD-route oriented rather than an atomic multi-member fanout-bus API.

## Snapshots

Captured AM62L SOC BYTE1 fanout, matched from 9.611899 mm to 8.499999 mm phase-local skew:

![AM62L SOC length matching](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/blob/feat/fanout-length-matching/tests/__snapshots__/am62l-soc-length-matching.snap.svg?raw=1)

Compact synthetic regression, matched from 1.112 mm to at most 0.25 mm:

![Length-matched fanout](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/blob/feat/fanout-length-matching/tests/__snapshots__/bus-length-matching.snap.svg?raw=1)

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`

title: Render PCBs in Altium's default layer order
description: Render PCB records using Altium Designers default Layer Drawing Order categories, allowing for accurate representation of PCB layers in SVG format.
body:
## Summary

- Render PCB records using Altium Designer's default Layer Drawing Order categories: Multi-Layer, overlays, connections, current layer, signal layers, paste, solder mask, internal planes, drill guide, keep-out, mechanical layers, drill drawing, and visible grids.
- Default the static SVG's current layer to Top Layer and add `currentLayer` for callers rendering another active layer.
- Keep `layerDrawingOrder` as a complete front-to-back override for customized Altium preferences.
- Keep selection, DRC, and hole indicators as system overlays and the background behind Altium's visible-grid category.
- Add one focused SVG test for the complete default order and one for Current Layer behavior, then refresh every affected real-board SVG snapshot.

## Why

Altium does not draw the PCB using the physical board stack as a universal z-order. Its PCB Editor preference defines a category-based Layer Drawing Order, with the first category rendered on top and the active layer assigned a dedicated Current Layer priority.

The previous implementation used a plausible front-view heuristic. This change instead follows the system default shown in [Altium's PCB Editor Display documentation](https://www.altium.com/documentation/altium-designer/preferences/pcb-editor), while still allowing callers to reproduce a customized preference exactly.

## Verification

title: Render schematic clock and inversion pin symbols
description: Renders schematic clock and inversion pin symbols in Altium, addressing previously ignored SVG fields for accurate representation.
body:
Altium schematic pins can store a clock triangle in `SYMBOL_INNEREDGE` and an inversion bubble in `SYMBOL_OUTEREDGE`. The SVG renderer ignored both fields, so source schematics silently lost those marks.

This renders the native fields directly at the pin body, shortens the line around inversion bubbles, and moves the pin number past either mark so text does not overlap it. It does not infer symbols from pin names or electrical types.

The focused snapshot covers all four pin directions and a combined inverted-clock pin. Existing TI reference snapshots prove the change on 29 real clock pins and 2 real inversion pins.

description: Add a schematic graphic element to Circuit JSON, allowing for user-provided system block diagrams on schematic sheets with optional asset and SVG content.

## Summary

- add a `schematic_graphic` Circuit JSON element
- allow an optional `asset` using the shared `Asset` schema (`project_relative_path`, `url`, and `mimetype`)
- allow optional `svg_content`, while requiring at least one of `asset` or `svg_content` when parsing

## Motivation

This is the Circuit JSON layer for placing a user-provided system block diagram on a schematic sheet, including the first page of a schematic PDF. A graphic may use an `asset`, inline `svg_content`, or both. When both are present, the asset is the canonical source reference and `svg_content` can carry cached/fallback content. Optional width and height define bounds centered inside the sheet, while omitted bounds preserve full-page behavior.

title: feat: support schematic sheet graphics
description: Add the schematicgraphic  intrinsic component and emit canonical schematic_graphic Asset records, supporting svgContent, imageUrl, or both, while enforcing SVG standards and improving schematic rendering.
body:
## Summary

- Add the `<schematicgraphic />` intrinsic component and emit canonical `schematic_graphic` Asset records.
- Support `svgContent`, `imageUrl`, or both. `imageUrl` is the canonical Asset source, while `svgContent` is an optional materialized fallback.
- Resolve project/static image paths through the platform while retaining the original `project_relative_path` and storing the resolved, fetchable Asset URL.
- Allow optional positive `width` and `height` props, emitted in schematic units and rendered as centered bounds.
- Keep inline `svgContent` assets Asset-only by default, materialize fetched external SVG content for synchronous rendering, and recover from failed external loads when explicit fallback content exists.
- Enforce canonical-source precedence for valid inline and fetched external assets, restrict `imageUrl` to SVG, and reject malformed inline data assets.
- Preserve first-page stacked-schematic behavior with a focused SVG snapshot and structural page-order coverage.
- Consume the broadened Circuit JSON contract where `asset` and `svg_content` are individually optional but at least one is required; Core deliberately continues emitting a canonical Asset for every prop source.
- Use the released renderer that emits one isolated SVG `<image>` data URL without parsing or rewriting the supplied SVG document.
- Preserve Core's automatic sheet naming/indexing while integrating current main's configurable sheet dimensions; refreshed snapshots now render their actual 500×300 and ANSI-B page sizes.

## Dependencies

- Props: `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.640` (released from merged [tscircuit/props#818](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/818))
- Circuit JSON: `circuit-json@^0.0.479` (released from merged [tscircuit/circuit-json#730](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/730))
- Renderer: `circuit-to-svg@^0.0.410` (released from merged [tscircuit/circuit-to-svg#695](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/695))
- Existing copper-pour preview is inherited unchanged from current `main`: `https://pkg.pr.new/@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver@85`

## Image-tag compatibility

- `svgContent` and SVG files supplied through `imageUrl` must be complete standalone SVG documents, including `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` on the root element.
- Browser SVG output keeps the complete document embedded in the image data URL. The committed stacked-schematic SVG snapshot is generated from a `<schematicsheet><schematicgraphic /></schematicsheet>` page-one fixture and contains linked `schematic_sheet`/`schematic_graphic` IDs plus the labeled block diagram in the embedded `href`.
- Tests also decode the emitted `href` and verify exact source content, including labels, source precedence, and page-one placement.
- The current `tsci` schematic-PDF path rasterizes with Resvg. Resvg renders shapes and paths from a nested SVG image but currently omits its `<text>` elements ([resvg#740](https://github.com/linebender/resvg/issues/740)). The SVG snapshot intentionally remains the inspectable source of truth for browser output, while decoded-content assertions protect its labels because the raster snapshot comparator cannot see them; CLI PDF label support needs a separate exporter follow-up.

## Bun 1.4 rationale

The full dependency graph reproducibly fails to resolve the existing copper-pour preview under Bun 1.3.14, while the same graph succeeds under Bun 1.4.0. The sharded test workflow uses Bun 1.4.0, and `vercel.json` uses Vercel's exact-version install command. The copper-pour dependency itself is unchanged from current `main`.

## Validation

- `bunx bun@1.4.0 test` — 1,477 passing, 40 skipped, 0 failing; 58 snapshots
- `bunx bun@1.4.0 test tests/features/schematic-sheet` — 19 passing
- focused nested graphic plus custom-dimension snapshots — 3 passing, 17 assertions
- `bunx bun@1.4.0 run smoke-test:dist`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx bun@1.4.0 run build`
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`
- Biome checks on changed TypeScript and package files
- confirmed installed `circuit-to-svg` is the released `0.0.410`
- confirmed the committed SVG snapshot orders `Sheet 1` → `schematic_graphic`/`image` → `Detailed Schematic` and preserves the exact embedded SVG document

## Summary

- model the documented physical package balls for all 16 AM62L-to-LPDDR4 DQ connections
- connect all 97 AM62L VSS balls and all 58 LPDDR4 VSS balls to the inner1 GND pour
- connect all 5 AM62L VDDS_DDR balls plus all 20 LPDDR4 VDDQ and 24 VDD2 balls to the shared 1.1 V VDD_LPDDR4 pour on inner2
- connect all 8 LPDDR4 VDD1 balls to their separate 1.8 V SOC_DVDD1V8 pour on inner3
- route all 212 plane drops and 32 DQ escapes through legal offset dogbones; via-in-pad remains disabled
- keep logical route transitions on their destination layers while inflating all 244 physical via barrels across the complete eight-layer stack
- enforce phase-local length matching on both DDR byte buses while preserving a straight, noncrossing global handoff
- propagate blind/buried-via policy through Board, imported Circuit JSON, nested board routing, SRJ, fanout planning, and autorouted pcb_via inflation
- consume the SRJ physical-span hint during via inflation without leaking it into persisted `pcb_trace.route`
- preserve the signal-only BGA solver comparison through the shared AM62L fixture

## Dependencies

- [tscircuit/fanout-solver#97](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/pull/97), released as `@tscircuit/fanout-solver@0.0.39`
- Use the live [copper-pour-solver#85](https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/pull/85) preview (`@85`) because the commit-addressed pkg.pr.new URL on current `main` does not resolve. A fresh install, TypeScript, and the focused repro pass with the live preview.

## Validation

- AM62L repro: 4,867 assertions, zero routing or clearance errors; snapshot-update run in 28.5s and stable rerun in 27.7s on the local M3 Pro
- phase-local length skew: BYTE0 7.532058 mm / 7.999999 mm; BYTE1 14.499999 mm / 14.499999 mm
- BYTE1 adds real tuning on both packages: one SOC trace and three DRAM traces; BYTE0 retains four DRAM-side tuned traces
- all 244 via renderings and all pad geometry remain unchanged; the global straight-line handoff remains unchanged and crossing-free
- BGA comparison: 329 assertions passed in signal-only mode
- focused via-policy and board-propagation suite: 8 tests passed
- seven affected fanout, copper-pour, winding, and SRJ snapshot tests passed after focused updates
- SRJ metadata persistence cleanup: 2 focused tests, 9 assertions
- exact solver captures: SOC 118 of 118 and RAM 126 of 126, each in one attempt with zero validation issues
- fresh install with the live copper-pour preview and `@tscircuit/fanout-solver@0.0.39`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit --pretty false`
- Core CI at `4cf81484`: all 10 Bun shards, Type Check, Format PR, Dependency Check, Smoke Test Dist, and Vercel passed

## Snapshot

Updated to show offset dogbone vias across both packages, three internal power planes, visible length matching on both DDR byte buses, and the straight global handoff. Every autorouted via is asserted outside its source-pad clearance and physically spans all eight layers.

title: feat: render schematic graphic assets
description: Render each schematic graphic as an outer g containing an SVG image hrefdata:imagesvgxml,...; circuit-to-svg no longer parses, injects, sanitizes, or rewrites the source SVG DOM.
body:
## Summary

- render each `schematic_graphic` as an outer `<g>` containing an SVG `<image href="data:image/svg+xml,...">`; circuit-to-svg no longer parses, injects, sanitizes, or rewrites the source SVG DOM
- pass a canonical inline SVG Asset data URL through unchanged, prefer it over `svg_content`, and embed caller-materialized `svg_content` for external Assets
- support `svg_content` without an Asset by encoding its UTF-8 bytes as a base64 SVG data URL
- retain clear errors for missing sources, non-SVG Assets, mismatched or malformed data URLs, raw fragment hashes, misplaced base64 metadata, and external Assets that have not been materialized
- preserve sheet selection and background layering, and center/clamp optional `width` and `height` within the inner-sheet or output viewport
- use each selected sheet's configured dimensions when fitting graphics, including custom-width/custom-height sheets
- rely on the SVG image-document boundary to isolate source CSS, classes, and repeated IDs instead of maintaining a parser/sanitizer dependency chain

## Input requirement

The embedded source must be a complete standalone SVG document. In particular, its root must declare `xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"`; Resvg renders an SVG image without that namespace as blank. circuit-to-svg intentionally does not parse or normalize the document under this architecture.

SVG image mode isolates the source document and disables scripts, interactivity, and external resource loading in browser renderers. Declarative SVG animation may still run when the generated SVG is viewed dynamically in a browser.

## Known CLI/PDF limitation

The current tscircuit CLI schematic-PDF path rasterizes circuit-to-svg output with Resvg 2.6.2. Resvg currently omits `<text>` inside SVG data-URL `<image>` elements ([linebender/resvg#740](https://github.com/linebender/resvg/issues/740)). Shapes render, and the exact text markup remains present in the embedded href, but diagram labels will be absent from CLI-generated schematic PDFs until the rasterizer is changed/fixed or text is converted to paths. Browser SVG rendering is not affected by this Resvg limitation.

The obsolete text visual snapshot was removed instead of being refreshed to a misleading textless image. A machine-visible TODO tracks the Resvg issue, structural tests verify the original text remains embedded, and a separate shape-only pixel test covers the supported Resvg output.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 341 passing, 1 TODO, 0 failing
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- focused coverage for percent/base64 hrefs, UTF-8 encoding, raw-hash rejection, base64 metadata ordering, Asset precedence, external fallback materialization, missing/invalid sources, sheet scoping, default and custom sheet dimensions, sizing/clamping/centering, layering, opaque parser-invalid content, SVG namespace rendering, source-style isolation, and repeated IDs

Implementation chain:

- props contract: tscircuit/props#818
- Circuit JSON schema: tscircuit/circuit-json#730 / `circuit-json@^0.0.479`
- core follow-up: tscircuit/core#3458

Immutable package preview of the schematic-graphic renderer before the custom-sheet integration: https://pkg.pr.new/circuit-to-svg@c8ef526

## Visual regression

- `tests/sch/__snapshots__/schematic-graphic-inside-sheet.snap.svg` snapshots a labeled system block diagram embedded as an opaque `<image>` inside its linked `schematic_sheet`, including the complete sheet frame and layering.

title: Fix passive one-port power and ground false positives
description: Exempts simple-chip packages with fewer than two connectable ports from power and ground pin presence checks, treating explicit do-not-connect package pads as non-connectable while keeping existing checks for multi-port chips.
body:
## Summary

- exempt simple-chip packages with fewer than two connectable ports from the power- and ground-pin presence checks
- treat explicit do-not-connect package pads as non-connectable
- keep all existing pin specification checks active for ordinary multi-port chips
- add an ANT1-style FEED plus NC regression and an active-chip control

## Why this boundary is safe

A one-port component cannot truthfully expose both a supply and a return pin. The exemption is limited to the two power/ground-presence checks; the general underspecified-pin check still runs, so a one-port chip must still describe its usable pin semantics.

This is narrower than and complementary to #211, which identifies interchangeable passive jumpers.

## Validation

title: fix: accept same-net copper at trace endpoints
description: Fixes false disconnected endpoint findings by allowing same-net copper connections at trace endpoints, improving trace continuity checks.
body:
## Stack

- Reproduction/base: #246
- This PR flips the four false disconnected-endpoint findings in that reproduction to zero.

## Root cause

The net-level branch of checkTracesAreContiguous only recognized endpoints touching pads. Region rerouting deliberately returns a replacement trace section whose endpoint copper overlaps retained same-net trace sections, so each valid join was reported as disconnected.

## Fix

- prove contact at the exact endpoint against same-layer trace segments on the same logical net
- use actual round-cap copper widths and a 1e-9 numeric tolerance, not coordinate equality
- keep contact local to the endpoint so a trace touching elsewhere cannot hide a floating end
- index candidates lazily by logical net and layer; fully padded routes pay no new preprocessing
- stay conservative for interpolated traces and vias, whose geometry/layer-span semantics need separate handling

Coverage includes T-junctions, shared source nets, wrong nets/layers, sub-micron near misses, short and closed traces, width changes, zero-length route points, and contact elsewhere along the owner trace.

## Validation

- full test suite: 220 pass, 0 fail
- TypeScript, ESM/DTS build, targeted Biome, and git diff check pass
- padded 1k/2k trace benchmarks show no regression

title: test: reproduce net-level trace join false positives
description: Reproduces false positives in net-level trace connectivity checks for regional reroute joins in PCB designs.
body:
## Summary

- add a minimal Circuit JSON reproduction for a regional reroute split across three physically continuous `pcb_trace` records
- keep all records on the same logical source trace while preserving the Arduino output's `0.0003 mm` boundary-coordinate rounding
- record the current four false `disconnected_endpoint_*` findings at the two copper-overlapping joins
- snapshot the retained copper, replacement section, and both physical joins

## Current behavior

`checkTracesAreContiguous` treats net-level trace endpoints as connected only when they touch a pad. It does not recognize direct contact with another same-net trace, so both sides of each valid regional-reroute join are reported as disconnected.

This is the shared-checker reproduction behind the Arduino Pipeline9 performance issue recorded in tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2232. The checker false positives cause Pipeline9 to run repeated reference-DRC repair evaluations even though the routed copper is continuous.

## Stack

This PR contains only the green reproduction. The shared continuity fix will be stacked on this branch.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repros/repro-net-level-region-reroute-continuity.test.ts`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit --pretty false`

title: Fix Pipeline9 preloaded via clearance regression
description: Fixes a regression in Pipeline9 that allowed preloaded routes to be rerouted too close to foreign board copper, leading to potential design rule violations.
body:
## Summary

- reject GrowShrink regional-fallback candidates that move a preloaded route via too close to foreign board copper
- validate again after force-improve and repair so later mutations cannot reintroduce the violation
- carry rejection statistics through Pipeline9 and let the existing GrowShrink lifecycle retry at a larger scale
- add a three-panel visual regression for the nRF QFN sibling-pad failure

## Root cause

Pipeline9 regional fallback could reroute established preloaded copper through a scale-one GrowShrink candidate without checking the candidate vias against board pad obstacles. On the nRF watch route this inserted a 0.6 mm RF via beside U1.P0_24. The downstream DRC repair saw the geometry but had no locally valid relocation.

The validator is scoped to movable preloaded connections, uses the SRJ via-to-pad clearance, checks actual via spans and rotated board obstacles, and preserves same-net exemptions through the connectivity map.

## Validation

- focused bugreport100 visual test: pass
- bunx tsc --noEmit: pass
- bun run build: pass
- git diff --check: pass
- reduced Pipeline9 watch replay: solved in about 10 seconds, one candidate rejected, scale 1 to 2 retry, RF remains top-only with zero vias
- current smart-watch clean replay: original P0_24 via regression absent; 113 unique traces and all routed vias remain 0.3 mm drill / 0.6 mm pad

## Visual review

Snapshot shows the clean preloaded RF route, the former fallback via colliding with a foreign QFN pad, and the fixed fallback result after candidate rejection.

title: Preserve explicit ground connections instead of redundant GND branches
description: Fixes the issue of redundant ground branches in the PGA300 circuit by preserving explicit ground connections and preventing unnecessary routing.
body:
## Context

The PGA300 reproduction from #930 is now merged into `main`. This PR is rebased onto the latest `main` (`5091d2f`) and contains one fix commit.

The global ground spanning tree was replacing the circuit's explicit PGA300 COMP–R1 ground wire with two unnecessary branches: COMP–U1.GND and COMP–C3.

## Fix

- Extend the existing `getGroundConnectionPolicy` path used by both the MSP and long-distance solvers.
- For nets explicitly marked `isGround`, preserve physical islands defined by explicit pin-to-pin traces.
- Treat label-only ground pins as separate physical islands and connect those islands electrically through labels rather than new routed traces.
- Prevent long-distance recovery from recreating the redundant ground branches.
- Keep existing automatic ground-bus behavior for unannotated nets and marked ground nets without explicit wires.
- Avoid circuit-specific pin IDs or coordinates in production code.

The full-circuit regression now requires the explicit COMP–R1 connection, rejects both redundant branches, verifies all source GND pins remain electrically connected through traces and labels, and preserves the vertical Q1–R1 connection.

## Before / after

### Before — merged reproduction

![Before: redundant PGA300 ground branches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/e51b3238f4fb800bad6263738c91db1cf7f0ea87/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-pga300-redundant-ground-traces.snap.svg)

### After — generated by this PR

![After: explicit COMP to R1 connection without redundant branches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/schematic-trace-solver/56fb3ea1a13c0b0be23e2dd205ccb0fbed0bab02/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-pga300-redundant-ground-traces.snap.svg)

## Validation

- `bun test`: **280 passed, 4 existing skips, 0 failures**
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- Focused Biome formatting check
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`

All checks above pass.

## Summary

- recover fallback labels on aligned multi-pin named nets
- bridge already-routed same-net components when their anchors and endpoints form one rail
- use authoritative `isGround` metadata instead of matching ground net ID strings
- preserve ground islands, intentional co-facing power branches, and the routed components' existing labels
- assert all six recovered example51 connections across NET_01, NET_03, NET_05, NET_08, BAT, and PPHV
- render semantic snapshot panels from the final net-label-to-trace stage so recovered traces appear in both views
- follow the tscircuit handbook's naming conventions and use explicit branches instead of ternary expressions

## Why

Named net metadata changed the original NET_03/NET_05 endpoints from direct-connection labels to named-net fallback labels, so the recovery stage filtered them out.

The remaining example51 gaps were different: each side was already routed locally, but the recovery stage only paired single-pin fallback labels. It never considered two disconnected routed components of the same named net.

Snapshot Circuit JSON also stopped at the earlier inline-label stage, leaving its lower semantic panel stale after trace recovery.

title: fix(schematic): preserve component field and net label placement
description: Fixes the issue where KiCad rearranges component fields and net labels, ensuring that their positions are preserved as specified in Circuit JSON.
body:
## Summary

- preserves Circuit JSON’s explicit placement for component fields by writing `fields_autoplaced no` for every exported symbol instance;
- preserves net-label anchors by disabling KiCad auto-placement for both regular global labels and label-backed symbols;
- adds a serialization assertion to `repro18` so every affected exported object remains explicitly positioned.

## Root cause

The converter calculated and wrote component-field positions and net-label anchor positions, but then marked the same KiCad objects as `fields_autoplaced`. KiCad treats that flag as permission to rearrange fields when the schematic is opened. That second placement pass can move text away from its Circuit JSON coordinates, causing footprint identifiers and net labels to crowd pins or lose their intended spacing.

## Fix

Set `fields_autoplaced` to `no` for exported schematic symbols and net labels. KiCad now retains the coordinates supplied by Circuit JSON instead of replacing them with automatic placement. This applies to every component symbol and label, not only the minimal fixture used by the reproduction.

## Test plan

- `bun test tests/sch/repros/repro18-footprint-net-label-alignment.test.tsx`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`

The local test exercised KiCad 10.0.5 successfully. The snapshot baseline remains the CI-generated Linux baseline so the pull-request workflow remains the final visual verification.

title: repro(schematic): component fields and net labels are misaligned in KiCad
description: Adds a visual regression test demonstrating that schematic text placement is not preserved when Circuit JSON is converted to KiCad, highlighting misalignment of component fields and net labels in the generated schematic.
body:
## Summary

Adds a focused visual regression test demonstrating that schematic text placement is not preserved when Circuit JSON is converted to KiCad.

The side-by-side snapshot shows the broader export problem: component fields, including the footprint identifier, and connected net labels are positioned correctly relative to the symbol in Circuit JSON, but appear displaced or inconsistently aligned in the generated KiCad schematic.

This is not specific to the component used in the fixture. The fixture is intentionally small so the mismatch is easy to see, but the same conversion behavior affects component symbols generally. Any schematic containing multiple components can therefore accumulate repeated label and field placement errors after export.

## Motivation

Schematic conversion should preserve readability as well as electrical connectivity. When component fields and net labels shift during export:

- labels can crowd pins, wires, or nearby text;
- footprint identifiers no longer maintain the intended spacing from their symbols;
- larger schematics require repetitive manual repositioning in KiCad;
- regenerated exports can undo that cleanup, making the workflow difficult to maintain;
- visual review becomes less reliable because the KiCad result no longer matches the source schematic layout.

A regression snapshot gives this systemic placement issue a stable, reviewable reproduction and provides a baseline for a follow-up fix without changing converter behavior in this PR.

## Test plan

- `bun test tests/sch/repros/repro18-footprint-net-label-alignment.test.tsx`
- `bunx biome check tests/sch/repros/repro18-footprint-net-label-alignment.test.tsx`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

title: Add INA350CDS chip and reusable instrumentation amplifier module
description: Add INA350  INA350CDSIDSGR with the DSG0008A WSON-8 footprint and exposed pad, along with a reusable InstrumentationAmplifier_INA350 module containing only the CDS IC and its 100 nF bypass capacitor, correcting previous grounding issues for the TIDA-010266 use case.
body:
## Summary

- Add `INA350` / `INA350CDSIDSGR` with the DSG0008A WSON-8 footprint and exposed pad. Retain the exact `INA350ABSIDSGR` export, sharing the same footprint definition.
- Add reusable `InstrumentationAmplifier_INA350` containing **only the CDS IC and its 100 nF bypass capacitor** (TIDA-010266 U5/C13). **No pin headers, connectors, or J10 gain jumper** are included.
- Keep REF external for the parent’s buffered 1.25 V reference. Expose GS and SHDN by default; CDS gain is 30 V/V with GS low and 50 V/V with GS high/open. SHDN high/open enables the device; low disables it.
- Support fixed `gain={30}` / `gain={50}` and `shutdown="enabled"`. Update exports, docs, the header-free import example, six snapshots, and regression tests.

The previous ABS-only implementation grounded REF; this revision corrects both points for the requested TIDA-010266 use case.

## Reference schematic

[TI TIDA-010266 / TIDUF53, Figure 4-1 (page 17)](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/tiduf53/tiduf53.pdf#page=17). The relevant stage is **U5 INA350CDSIDSGR + C13**. J10 is an optional gain-selection jumper on the parent board.

![TI TIDA-010266 reference schematic, including INA350CDSIDSGR U5 and C13](https://www.ti.com/ods/images/TIDUF53/GUID-20231204-SS0I-WWGZ-JTG0-ZP5LHS9HJ7WJ-low.svg)

Pinout, gain selection, and shutdown behavior: [INA350 datasheet, Table 6-1](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina350.pdf#page=4).

## Implemented module

![INA350CDS reusable module schematic with external REF, GS, and SHDN](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/ca2ff97791e1c3f526762799d79c2b0536a2b0d6/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/InstrumentationAmplifier_INA350.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)

The parent provides supply, reference generator, sensor, ADC/filter, and any controls. The example connects named parent nets without physical connectors; routing is disabled there until actual application components terminate the nets. REF is not tied to ground, and SHDN is not pulled low.

## Validation

- `bun test tests`: **17 passed, 0 failed**.
- `bun run typecheck`: passed.
- Biome formatting check on all nine changed TypeScript files: passed.
- Header-free example CLI build: passed with no circuit error records (parts engine disabled).
- Routed integration tests: external gain control, gain 30, and gain 50; all interface pins connected to test-only parent endpoints.
- Tests verify exactly two module components, CDS/ABS pinouts and footprints, external REF/SHDN isolation, and isolation between two imported modules.
- Refreshed schematic/PCB snapshots and visually reviewed them.

## Notes

Use 1.8–5.5 V supply and meet the datasheet input/common-mode/output limits. Fixed gain 50 uses a bottom-layer gain strap with two vias to preserve SHDN clearance; the module uses 0.1 mm traces and requires final parent-board DRC/fabrication review.

The CLI still warns about missing schematic-sheet/pin metadata. No analog simulation or medical-device validation is claimed. Unrelated local work is excluded.

body:
## Summary

- coordinate fixed interstitial dogbone sites across multiple signal buses and dense singleton plane drops
- preserve per-layer winding constraints while trying bounded cross-layer interleavings
- length-match dense fanout prefixes only when the remaining plane dogbones still have a complete legal assignment
- bound route diversity and multi-span meander search to avoid combinatorial growth
- add a captured AM62L SoC phase repro with a focused functional/DRC/SVG regression and an interactive debugger page

This is the solver support needed by the AM62L/LPDDR4 Core regression with two byte buses, an 8-signal address/control bus, 212 plane drops, dogbones, and through-all vias.

## Repro

`tests/am62l-lpddr4-three-bus-through-all-repro.test.ts` exercises the self-contained SoC fanout phase:

- 126 connections and 373 active AM62L BGA pads
- 102 singleton power-plane drops plus three 8-signal boundary buses
- 8 layers, via-in-pad disabled, blind/buried vias disabled
- one full-stack dogbone via per connection
- BYTE0/BYTE1/ADDR_CTRL skew limits of 8/14.5/15 mm

The predecessor did not complete this fixture within a 45-second cutoff. This branch completes it in about 18 seconds locally, validates all 126 traces, and passes independent routed-copper DRC. The same fixture is available interactively at `repros/repro03-am62l-three-bus-through-all.page.tsx`; it does not auto-run.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- focused AM62L repro: 1 test, 981 assertions, stable SVG snapshot (17.5–18.5 s across repeated runs)
- focused solver set: 10 tests, 422 assertions (9 initially passed; the only delta was the expected layered-winding SVG, refreshed and rerun green)
- Core AM62L/LPDDR4 three-bus integration: 5,045 assertions, ~51.2 s test body / ~52.0 s wall
- isolated phase solves:
  - SoC: 126/126 connections, ~18.2 s
  - RAM: 134/134 connections, ~26.4 s
- measured local skews:
  - SoC BYTE0 7.175 mm, BYTE1 14.191 mm, ADDR_CTRL 13.613 mm
  - RAM BYTE0 8.000 mm, BYTE1 14.500 mm, ADDR_CTRL 15.000 mm

The broad suite is left to hosted CI to avoid overloading the development machine after an earlier crash.

body:
## Summary

- assign component-wide legal dogbone via sites before routing dense mixed signal and plane fanouts
- keep route transitions logical while modeling through-all physical barrels when blind and buried vias are disabled
- require explicit SimpleRouteJson allowViaInPad true before using via-in-pad
- preserve one-via winding and bus length matching outside the dense pad boundary
- bound winding-order search and spatially index via and obstacle clearance checks

## Why

The AM62L and LPDDR4 packages contain hundreds of power-plane drops alongside two ordered byte buses. Source-centered vias violated the board policy, while greedy dogbones could strand either the byte buses or nearby plane pads. The component-wide assignment reserves legal interstitial dogbones for the complete package and routes the buses around those fixed through-all barrels.

## Validation

- full CI: 110 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed; 111,705 assertions
- TypeScript compilation, format check, and Vercel checks
- 15 focused tests, 422 assertions
- bounded layered-winding and SRJ29 snapshot refresh
- exact SOC capture: 118 of 118 routed, one attempt, zero validation issues
- exact RAM capture: 126 of 126 routed, one attempt, zero validation issues

title: Render schematic hierarchy blocks and sheet entries
description: Renders the native records that make up Altium schematic hierarchy blocks, ensuring they are visible in native source previews and converted previews.
body:
## Summary

Renders the native records that make up Altium schematic hierarchy blocks:

- `RECORD=15`: sheet symbol body
- `RECORD=16`: sheet entry
- `RECORD=32`: sheet name
- `RECORD=33`: sheet filename

AltiumTS already parsed these records, but its SVG serializer skipped them. As a result, hierarchy blocks disappeared from native source previews and converted previews even when the Altium documents were correct.

## Implementation

- Uses each sheet symbol's native position and size.
- Places each owned entry from its native side and distance fields.
- Uses the document font table for sheet text.
- Uses each entry's native `TEXTFONTID` for its label.
- Keeps the hierarchy renderer and font lookup in focused modules instead of expanding the main SVG serializer.
- Uses the existing schematic component palette for hierarchy blocks.

## Why this belongs in AltiumTS

The converter was already writing the hierarchy records correctly. Changing the converter or post-processing its SVG would leave native Altium source previews broken and would hide the actual renderer omission.

This change only renders the four hierarchy record kinds above. It does not alter wire geometry, net connectivity, or record ordering. In particular, the floating blue wire stubs visible in the converter's HERON PAY-SSM snapshot are native `RECORD=27` records from the source schematic; they are not created by this change.

## Verification

- Focused SVG snapshot with one hierarchy block and input/output entries.
- Existing open-source Elk Pi SVG snapshot.
- `bun run format`
- `bun run lint`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test tests/svg/schematic-sheet-symbol.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/svg/elk-pi-main-sheet.test.ts`
- `bun run build`
- GitHub `Bun Test` workflow passed the complete CI suite.

The optional TI reference bundle is not part of this checkout, so its large fixture tests were not included in the local verification above.

title: Preserve schematic No ERC markers and hierarchy blocks
description: Preserves native Altium No ERC markers through conversion and makes hierarchy blocks visible in the existing sourceconverted SVG comparisons.
body:
## Summary

Preserves native Altium No ERC markers through conversion and makes hierarchy blocks visible in the existing source/converted SVG comparisons.

- Applies the existing `source_port.do_not_connect` property after hierarchical sheet-entry ports have been created.
- Preserves standalone No ERC markers without adding a visible port symbol or changing the Circuit JSON schema.
- Writes sheet-entry No ERC markers at their native Altium positions.
- Pins AltiumTS `main` at `a6ef9bf303f150107b9a83307df67b262c557083`, which contains merged [AltiumTS #68](https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/pull/68), to render native sheet symbols, sheet entries, sheet names, and sheet filenames.
- Updates the existing HERON PAY-SSM, HERON Systems, and multi-sheet snapshots through Bun's SVG matcher.

## Why

No ERC records were previously processed before hierarchical sheet entries existed, and standalone markers had no internal representation. PAY-SSM therefore lost all 22 markers, while HERON Systems preserved only 8 of 10.

The missing hierarchy blocks were a separate renderer bug. Both the source and converted Altium documents already contained the records, but AltiumTS did not render:

- `RECORD=15`: sheet symbol
- `RECORD=16`: sheet entry
- `RECORD=32`: sheet name
- `RECORD=33`: sheet filename

This hid 16 sheet symbols and 94 entries in PAY-SSM, and 7 sheet symbols and 34 entries in HERON Systems, on both sides of the comparison.

The converter continues to use the existing `do_not_connect` property, and every output position comes from native Altium geometry. The SVG snapshots are not edited, injected, or transformed.

## Roundtrip 2 wire stubs

The short blue segments around labels such as `A_PHASE_MOT1`, `ADC1_CS_N`, and `PEX_CS` are native top-level Altium wire records (`RECORD=27`) with net labels (`RECORD=25`). They already exist in the HERON PAY-SSM source and are intentionally preserved. They are not missing component bodies and are not introduced by either fix in this PR.

## Verification

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 49 tests passed across 49 files with 541 assertions.
- One focused test file covers standalone No ERC round trips.
- One focused test file covers sheet-entry No ERC placement.
- Inspected both real-board source/output SVG pairs at full resolution.
- PAY-SSM preserves 22 of 22 No ERC markers; HERON Systems preserves 10 of 10.
- Hierarchy blocks and entries are visible on both sides of both real-board comparisons.

## Summary

- Adds deterministic, bounded all-direction power/GND via-line generation with continuous top-path and all-layer through-via clearance checks.
- Adds minimum-conflict signal ViaLine relocation and local tail repair for expanded real breakout-point spacing while preserving unaffected escapes.
- Applies octilinear miter normalization, exact endpoint validation, through-via enforcement, and no-via-in-pad clearance checks to repaired routes.
- Retains the best physically valid 33-signal solution when bounded co-routing retries time out, fail, or regress power coverage, with structured unresolved-cluster diagnostics.
- Adds captured 1.25x SoC/RAM fixtures and a bounded Cosmos page with clean PCB visualization.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- Best-valid fallback regression
- General via-line rotation and non-nearest legal-event regression
- Common source-net normalization detecting all 58 RAM VSS pads
- Exact 1.25x RAM miter and endpoint regression
- Expanded SoC/RAM minimal-tail repair regression
- Captured SoC/RAM outward-edge power regression
- Fixed RAM 33-route regression
- Pipeline lifecycle and granular visualization regressions

## Full-board consumer result

The isolated 1.25x consumer routes all 33 DDR mappings end-to-end and passes endpoint coincidence, via-in-pad, top-to-bottom through-via, minimum-clearance, and all-layer Gerber shorts checks. It connects 151/155 GND pads, versus 152/155 for the preserved baseline, so the baseline remains selected and the expanded-spacing consumer remains a diagnostic candidate rather than replacing the best board.

title: Add PCB keepout outlines
description: Extends the existing pcb_keepout element to support outline shapes, allowing for the preservation of stroked Track or Arc boundaries in PCB designs.
body:
## Why

Altium can define a keepout as a stroked Track or Arc boundary. The existing `pcb_keepout` element only represented rectangles and circles, so these boundaries could not be preserved without changing their geometry or meaning.

These boundaries are outlines rather than polygons: many are open, and their interior is not a filled keepout region.

## What changed

- Extend the existing `pcb_keepout` element with `shape: "outline"`
- Store its geometry in `outline` and preserve its `stroke_width`
- Require at least two outline points

This does not introduce another Circuit JSON element. It adds the missing outline geometry to the existing keepout element.

## Validation

- `bun test --max-concurrency=1` — 316 pass
- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
