title: fix: keep networked routes JSON-safe
description: Fixes serialization issues in networked routes by omitting absent jumper arrays and ensuring fixed-width responses for multi-head routes, maintaining route trust boundaries.
body:
## Summary

- omit absent jumper arrays from grown/shrunk and same-root repaired routes
- accept the multi-head solver's established fixed 0.15 mm route width at the network trust boundary without changing its geometry
- add focused regressions for JSON-safe routes, fixed-width responses, and the existing via-clearance behavior

## Why

The released Pipeline9 network-cache benchmark found two deterministic fail-open classes:

- repaired routes contained an own `jumpers: undefined`, so the exact cache correctly refused to serialize them
- multi-head routes legitimately used their established 0.15 mm width while the input requested 0.1 mm, so the client correctly rejected them under its narrower allowlist

Changing the multi-head solver to 0.1 mm altered route geometry and regressed the existing sibling-pad via-clearance reproduction. This revision keeps the released local routing semantics and extends the strict response allowlist only to the known 0.15 mm candidate width.

Four SRJ18 sample-13 A01 results still contain one-point routes that omit a distinct endpoint 0.1768 mm away. Those remain intentionally rejected and fail open to the local solver; accepting them would weaken the route trust boundary.

## Validation

- 22 focused Pipeline9 Networked, grow/shrink, repair, and via-clearance tests pass (222 expectations)
- the previously failing `bugreport100-nrf-endpoint-via-sibling-pad` test passes
- TypeScript typecheck passes
- package build passes
- exact projected-input diagnostics found no input validation errors or solver throws; all known JSON serialization failures are covered by the jumper fixes
- `git diff --check` passes

Validation 1818 Pipeline9 Networked tests, 205 assertions focused output regressions: 22 TypeScript check and build pass direct isolated SRJ18 samples 1, 2, 7, 11: end-to-end total 614.6s to 577.0s (6.1 faster); high-density total 225.1s to 192.7s (14.4 faster) exact completion, via-count, and relaxed-DRC parity in the paired benchmark The current deployed 0.0.852 cache still containsencounters the two pre-existing output defects, including a sample-11 regression. This PR fixes those causes; the next exact version receives a fresh versioned cache-key prefix.
body:
## Summary

- batch speculative Pipeline9 high-density cache lookups into streaming NDJSON requests
- pack at most 100 items and 1.75 MiB per batch, with exact UTF-8 accounting
- resolve items independently and out of order while preserving Pipeline9's sequential consumption semantics
- fan explicit cache misses out through parallel legacy `/solve` requests
- retain per-node logical timeouts, longer background transport timeouts, and fail-open local solving
- expose batch, item, byte, cache-miss, hit, solver, and fallback-reason counters to benchmarks
- fix two pre-existing outputs that prevented exact cache reuse: `jumpers: undefined` and the closed-form solver's incorrect trace thickness

The Networked pipeline remains available only at `effort: 1`, and every cache identity remains scoped to the exact autorouter package version.

## Protocol

`POST /solve-batch` accepts `{ autorouterVersion, items: [{ requestId, input }] }` and streams one NDJSON line per item. Cache hits are consumed immediately. A `CACHE_MISS` line launches that item through `/solve` without blocking the rest of the batch.

The backward-compatible service side is in [hd-cache2 PR #2](https://github.com/tscircuit/hd-cache2.tscircuit.com/pull/2) and is deployed.

## Validation

- 18/18 Pipeline9 Networked tests, 205 assertions
- focused output regressions: 2/2
- TypeScript check and build pass
- direct isolated SRJ18 samples 1, 2, 7, 11: end-to-end total 614.6s to 577.0s (6.1% faster); high-density total 225.1s to 192.7s (14.4% faster)
- exact completion, via-count, and relaxed-DRC parity in the paired benchmark

The current deployed 0.0.852 cache still contains/encounters the two pre-existing output defects, including a sample-11 regression. This PR fixes those causes; the next exact version receives a fresh versioned cache-key prefix.

## Summary

- add an effort-1-only `AutoroutingPipelineSolver9_Networked`
- launch exact high-density node cache requests in parallel while preserving Pipeline9's sequential fixed-copper fallback semantics
- fail open to the local ordinary solver on network, timeout, version, or protocol errors
- export an exact-version server helper and cache request/response contracts

- keep cold remote solves alive in the background after the 30s logical fallback, with a 310s transport cap

- client sends the exact `AUTOROUTER_VERSION`
- remote solving is available only at `effort: 1`
- cached solved and deterministic failed results follow the same ordinary-node fallback behavior as local Pipeline9
- fixed-copper/B01 nodes still use Pipeline9's existing sequential behavior; their speculative request can warm the cache but is not consumed

title: fix: preserve vias between overlapping single-layer pads
description: Fixes via removal issue when moving single-layer terminals onto overlapping same-net pads on another layer, ensuring connectivity is preserved during autorouting.
body:
## Summary

- pass authoritative PCB-port terminal layers into Pipeline9 trace simplification
- prevent via removal from moving an explicitly single-layer terminal onto an overlapping same-net pad on another layer
- preserve terminal PCB-port identities through every simplification iteration while retaining multilayer-terminal and crossing-via optimizations
- add a fast bidirectional simplifier regression and visual snapshot

## Root cause

Pipeline9 stitching produced the correct top-to-bottom routes and terminal vias for SRJ18 sample 9. During the first trace-simplification via-removal phase, a bottom-layer pad from another terminal on the same net was accepted as proof that the top-only `pcb_port_16` endpoint could move to bottom. The simplifier removed the required via and left the endpoint disconnected.

The checks continuity implementation in https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/249 exposed this real missing connection; it did not cause the routing defect.

The layer guard applies only when Pipeline9 has authoritative PCB-port metadata. It combines each connection point's declared layers with physical layers only when one exactly centered obstacle itself spans multiple layers. This retains plated-hole/MLCP via removal while preventing coincident or merely overlapping single-layer pads from impersonating a multilayer terminal, even though SRJ `connectedTo` contains whole-net identities. Routes without authoritative metadata keep the existing obstacle-based behavior.

## Validation

- 41 targeted via-removal, trace-simplification, crossing-via, and Pipeline9 mutation tests pass
- SRJ18 sample 9 exact-reference regression passes against the checks #249 implementation
- the existing multilayer-terminal test still removes an unnecessary via with explicit two-layer terminal metadata
- an exact-coincident top/bottom pad regression proves whole-net `connectedTo` identities cannot synthesize a fake multilayer terminal
- SRJ23 sample 3 output traces and SVG are byte-for-byte identical to `origin/main` after accounting for its centered plated-hole obstacles
- existing `bugreport05-f03221` and `repro117-standalone-simple-route` SVG snapshots remain unchanged
- TypeScript, build, repository format, and diff checks pass
- visual SVG snapshot included

body:
## Summary

- capture the exact four-layer CM5 maker-carrier SimpleRouteJson produced by tscircuit at 1x effort, including its routed output
- add an interactive Pipeline7 debugger fixture that reroutes from the same 30 connections and 318 obstacles with no cache, no preloaded copper, and allowViaInPad=false
- record the deterministic reference-DRC baseline for both the captured output and a fresh solve
- separate three Circuit JSON conversion alias artifacts from the twelve legitimate reference violations
- record the three additional real via-in-pad violations at CC1, SD_CLK, and SD_DAT0

## Current behavior

The full tscircuit build reports 41 records because several physical sites are represented by both generic and typed errors. In the autorouter repository reference checker, the captured and freshly routed outputs each produce 15 records: 11 trace, 3 via-trace, and 1 pad-trace. Three trace records are known same-net alias artifacts in the test conversion, leaving 12 legitimate reference violations. The route also places three terminal vias inside real CM5 pads even though via-in-pad is disabled.

The fixture deliberately retains the captured 141 traces and 132 vias for inspection; the debugger and solver test strip those traces before rerouting, so this is a true input reproduction rather than a pre-routed workaround.

## Stack

This is the reproduction base.

- stacked router fix: #2252
- SRJ producer prerequisite: tscircuit/core#3485

## Validation

- bun test tests/bugs/cm5-maker-carrier-drc.test.ts --timeout 9999999
- bunx tsc --noEmit --pretty false
- bun run build
- git diff --check

body:
## Summary

- add native tscircuit modules for the **Radar front end & processing** subsystem (TI obstacle-detection sensor subsystem **21581**)
- model the exact TIDEP-01024 devices used by the extracted reference: `AWR1843ARBGALPQ1`, `FW4000044Q`, `MX25V1635FZNQ`, and `CHS-01TA`
- reproduce the AWR1843AoP I/O, AOP power, 40 MHz crystal, QSPI flash, and SOP-option sections as native TSX
- export the reusable composite as `RadarFrontEndProcessing` and keep `examples/ObstacleDetectionSensor.circuit.tsx` intentionally minimal
- keep the TI reference ID in provenance comments, documentation, tests, and this PR description rather than production component or filename identifiers
- preserve native symbols, real ports, real `<trace from=... to=...>` connectivity, and native schematic autorouting

This implementation does **not** use numeric `schSize`, manual trace paths, route hints, embedded source files, screenshots, SVG overlays, or decorative/fake traces.

## Production naming

| Kind | Production name |
|---|---|
| Chip components | `AWR1843ARBGALPQ1`, `FW4000044Q`, `MX25V1635FZNQ`, and `CHS01TA` (verified manufacturer MPN `CHS-01TA`) |
| Child subcircuits | `RadarSoc_AWR1843ARBGALPQ1`, `RadarClock_FW4000044Q`, and `RadarQspiFlash_MX25V1635FZNQ` |
| Composite subcircuit | `RadarFrontEndProcessing` |
| Application example | `ObstacleDetectionSensor` |

The TI reference ID is intentionally absent from production component names, package exports, and production filenames. `TIDEP-01024` remains only in source provenance comments, source links, documentation, test context where useful, and this PR description.

## System block and authoritative sources

- [TI obstacle-detection sensor system block — variant 35081, subsystem 21581](https://www.ti.com/solution/obstacle-detection-sensor?variantid=35081&subsystemid=21581#block-diagram)
- [TIDEP-01024 reference-design page](https://www.ti.com/tool/TIDEP-01024)
- [TIDEP-01024 design guide — TIDUEZ2](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/tiduez2)
- [Editable Altium CAD archive — TIDM846](https://www.ti.com/lit/zip/tidm846)
- [Schematic, assembly, and BOM archive — SPRR429](https://www.ti.com/lit/zip/sprr429)
- [AWR1843AoP datasheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/awr1843aop.pdf)
- [Related conventions/example PR #129 — currently open](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/pull/129)

The implementation is Altium-backed. The downloaded `tidm846.zip` archive was inspected before use and contains the editable TIDEP-01024 database. The `sprr429.zip` archive was also inspected and contains the released schematic PDF, assembly drawings, and BOM.

## Extracted source files and functional sections

Primary editable schematic sources:

- `TIDEP-01024_Database/PROC106A1_AOP_IO.SchDoc`
  - 40 MHz crystal
  - AWR1843AoP I/O units
  - GPADC test points
  - I/O pull resistors and reset test point
  - SOP0/SOP1/SOP2 option networks
- `TIDEP-01024_Database/PROC106A1_AOP_PWR.SchDoc`
  - AWR1843AoP supply units
  - exact decoupling-capacitor groups and supply labels
- `TIDEP-01024_Database/PROC106A1_FLASH_USB_TO_UART.SchDoc`
  - QSPI flash section

Cross-check sources:

- `AWR1843AOPEVM Schematic, Assembly, and BOM/RevA1/PROC106A1(001)_Sch.PDF`
- `AWR1843AOPEVM Schematic, Assembly, and BOM/RevA1/PROC106A1(001)_BOM.xls`
- `AWR1843AOPEVM Schematic, Assembly, and BOM/RevA1/PROC106A1(001)_Assy.PDF`

## Coordinate transformations

The source placement is preserved through documented transforms:

- AWR1843AoP sheets:
  - `schX = (AltiumX - 850) * 0.01778`
  - `schY = (AltiumY - 550) * 0.0254` on AOP I/O
  - `schY = (AltiumY - 550) * 0.01778` on AOP power
- 40 MHz crystal section:
  - `schX = (sourceX - 275) * 0.0254`
  - `schY = (sourceY - 870) * 0.0254`
- QSPI flash section:
  - `schX = (sourceX - 500) * 0.06096`
  - `schY = (sourceY - 290) * 0.06096`

The differing uniform scales fit the wider ANSI-B source sheets into native A4 schematic sheets while retaining source-relative component placement. The AOP I/O pull-resistor bank uses the documented local vertical spacing adjustment required by native symbol label bounds; its source X coordinates and ordering remain unchanged.

## Main files

- `lib/chips/AWR1843ARBGALPQ1.circuit.tsx`
- `lib/chips/FW4000044Q.circuit.tsx`
- `lib/chips/MX25V1635FZNQ.circuit.tsx`
- `lib/chips/CHS01TA.circuit.tsx`
- `lib/subcircuits/RadarSoc_AWR1843ARBGALPQ1.circuit.tsx`
- `lib/subcircuits/RadarClock_FW4000044Q.circuit.tsx`
- `lib/subcircuits/RadarQspiFlash_MX25V1635FZNQ.circuit.tsx`
- `lib/subcircuits/RadarFrontEndProcessing.circuit.tsx`
- `examples/ObstacleDetectionSensor.circuit.tsx`
- `tests/RadarFrontEndProcessing.test.tsx`
- schematic snapshots for the standalone modules, composite, and example

Generated native snapshots can be inspected directly on the branch:

- [AWR1843AoP I/O and power sheets](https://github.com/AnasSarkiz/ti/blob/feat/obstacle-radar-21581/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/RadarSoc_AWR1843ARBGALPQ1.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)
- [40 MHz crystal](https://github.com/AnasSarkiz/ti/blob/feat/obstacle-radar-21581/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/RadarClock_FW4000044Q.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)
- [QSPI flash](https://github.com/AnasSarkiz/ti/blob/feat/obstacle-radar-21581/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/RadarQspiFlash_MX25V1635FZNQ.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)
- [composite radar front end](https://github.com/AnasSarkiz/ti/blob/feat/obstacle-radar-21581/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/RadarFrontEndProcessing.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)

## Side-by-side reference comparisons

These PNGs were regenerated from commit `22e6c47568fa5a48ec4078ddc1e789aa784028d0` after the QSPI sheet-boundary correction and the AOP I/O on-trace-label update.

### 40 MHz crystal

![TI reference and native tscircuit 40 MHz crystal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnasSarkiz/ti/22e6c47568fa5a48ec4078ddc1e789aa784028d0/docs/reference-comparisons/TIDEP01024/radar-clock-reference-vs-tscircuit.png)

### QSPI flash

![TI reference and native tscircuit QSPI flash](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnasSarkiz/ti/22e6c47568fa5a48ec4078ddc1e789aa784028d0/docs/reference-comparisons/TIDEP01024/radar-qspi-reference-vs-tscircuit.png)

### AWR1843 AOP I/O

![TI reference and native tscircuit AWR1843 AOP I/O](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnasSarkiz/ti/22e6c47568fa5a48ec4078ddc1e789aa784028d0/docs/reference-comparisons/TIDEP01024/radar-aop-io-reference-vs-tscircuit.png)

## Connectivity and visual validation

- validates all 180 unique AWR1843AoP balls, including multi-unit package rendering
- validates the crystal load capacitors and case-ground connections
- validates the QSPI series paths, pull resistors, decoupling, ground, and supply islands
- validates the composite public interfaces and its SoC/QSPI connectivity
- verifies the CHS-01TA standalone export and default reference designator
- compared the TI source and native tscircuit snapshots side by side at full-sheet and focused-section zoom levels
- checked the SOP networks against the extracted Altium centers and pin directions: 13 components, zero center error, zero pin-direction mismatches
- confirmed the radar implementation contains no numeric `schSize`, route hints, manual paths, or custom trace routing

## Commands run

- `bun install`
- `bun run format:check` — passed
- `bun run typecheck` — passed
- `bun test tests/RadarFrontEndProcessing.test.tsx` — 5 passed, 0 failed
- `bun test tests` — 40 passed, 0 failed
- `bunx tsci snapshot lib/subcircuits/RadarFrontEndProcessing.circuit.tsx --schematic-only --disable-parts-engine` — matched
- `bunx tsci snapshot examples/ObstacleDetectionSensor.circuit.tsx --schematic-only --disable-parts-engine` — matched
- `bun run build` — 206 circuits passed, exit code 0 before the final upstream sync

The repository-wide build still reports existing library-wide footprint/network/PCB diagnostics. The radar deliverable is schematic-focused, and its focused tests render with PCB and routing disabled and assert that no Circuit JSON errors are produced. The native full-sheet schematic autorouter completed the radar composite with 237 routed traces, zero jumpers, and zero schematic routing errors.

## Known native-renderer limitations

- the exact source-positioned left-edge GND symbol produces a sheet-bound warning in the CLI because its native label bounds extend slightly beyond the A4 drawing boundary; moving it would reduce source-placement fidelity
- full composite native autorouting is slow because the AWR1843AoP sheet has a large multi-unit symbol and many real connections
- no local rendering hacks were added for these limitations

title: Add TIDA-020027 TLIN1028 communication interface
description: Add native TLIN10283DDARQ1 and TLIN1028 chip components with the TI DDA PowerPAD pin map and a new LIN communication interface extracted from the TIDA-020027 reference design.
body:
## Summary

- add native `TLIN10283DDARQ1` and `TLIN1028` chip components with the TI DDA PowerPAD pin map
- add `CommunicationInterface_LIN_TLIN1028`, extracted from the **Power & LIN** block of TI TIDA-020027
- use the project runtime `tscircuit 0.0.2460` and native `trace` → `net.*` connections, including the valid `V3_3` power net
- preserve the source component centers with the documented transform `schX = (sourceX - 390) * 0.0254`, `schY = (sourceY - 380) * 0.0254`
- use native default passive schematic symbols, add exports, update the README catalog, and add the focused schematic snapshot

## Why LIN / why this reference

The Automotive Window Module subsystem page does not attach a reference design, so this implementation uses TI's official [TIDA-020027 automotive full-featured side-mirror/door-motor reference design](https://www.ti.com/tool/TIDA-020027). It is a body-motor design with downloadable native Altium source and uses TLIN1028-Q1, one of the system-basis devices listed for the requested subsystem.

The authoritative `SideMirror_Logic_TLIN1028.SchDoc` design contains a LIN interface only. No CAN interface is added.

This complements the motor-driver work in [PR #116](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/pull/116).

## Official source set

- [TIDA-020027 design page](https://www.ti.com/tool/TIDA-020027)
- [Altium CAD/CAE package (TIDM683)](https://www.ti.com/lit/zip/tidm683)
- [schematic PDF (TIDM679)](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/tidm679)
- [BOM (TIDM680)](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/tidm680)
- [design guide (TIDUES6)](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/tidues6)
- [TLIN1028-Q1 datasheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlin1028-q1.pdf)

## Reference vs generated schematic

### TI Altium reference — TIDA-020027 “Power & LIN”

Official PDF export of the `SideMirror_Logic_TLIN1028.SchDoc` sheet:

![TI TIDA-020027 Altium Power and LIN reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/9fcaf024e1f69c76b5f465788593c6e45f64c610/.github/pr-assets/129/tida-020027-power-and-lin-reference.png)

### Generated tscircuit schematic

![Generated CommunicationInterface_LIN_TLIN1028 schematic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/7f85d4319c1e6bfd3a70cb09423e97be561f1d3e/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/CommunicationInterface_LIN_TLIN1028.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)

## Extracted scope

The subcircuit reproduces U4 `TLIN10283DDARQ1`, C23/C24/C25/C26/C29/C31, and R19/R20 with the source refdes, values, ratings, footprints, pin mapping, labels, and connectivity. Passive manufacturer part numbers are intentionally omitted per repository convention.

The source's **Power & LIN** block has no discrete LIN TVS/ESD part. Its bus protection is the TLIN1028-Q1's integrated LIN protection, with C29 (220 pF) as the source's bus shunt capacitor. D2 (`SMAJ36CA`) and J4 are in the separate **MAIN SUPPLY** block, so they are outside this extraction; `Vsup`, `LIN`, and the logic signals remain native subcircuit boundaries. No PCB content is added.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check` — pass
- `bun run typecheck` — pass
- focused `tsci` snapshot update — pass and idempotent with `tscircuit 0.0.2460` / `@tscircuit/core 0.0.1752`
- `bun run build` — pass (`130 passed`, exit 0; existing repository warnings remain)
- focused Circuit JSON inspection — valid `V3_3` power net and no schematic connectivity error
- generated schematic visually compared with TIDM679 page 2

## Rendering/routing defect (separate)

The schematic renderer can physically draw an extra long connection between separate same-net GND labels after one branch contains a local multi-port trace. The Circuit JSON connectivity is correct, and the implementation does not hide the renderer defect with decorative lines or invented wiring.

Minimized upstream repro: [tscircuit/core#3436](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/3436)

title: Add TIDA-01389 Hall position-feedback subsystem
description: Add TIDA-01389 Hall position-feedback subsystem, reusing the DRV5013ADQDBZRQ1 chip definition and implementing the Hall channels with associated circuitry for position feedback in automotive applications.
body:
## Summary

- reuse main's shared `DRV5013ADQDBZRQ1` / `DRV5013Q1` chip definition with the DBZ SOT-23 data-sheet pinout
- add `PositionFeedback_DRV5013`, containing both TIDA-01389 Hall channels (U6/HALL_1 and U5/HALL_2), their C13/C14 decoupling, R14/R15 pull-ups, VCC/GND, and the relevant J1/J2/J4 + R9 connector circuitry
- restore J4 at its source center above J1/J2, with pin 2 on the source `+V_BAT` rail and pin 1 on GND
- render both source section boundaries with native dashed schematic boxes and outward native-text clearance, without changing passive dimensions or component centers
- connect Hall-channel and connector GND pins with ordinary `trace` declarations to `net.GND`, allowing tscircuit to generate native GND symbols; V_BAT remains native inline trace text
- export the chip and subcircuit, add focused SVG snapshots, and add 91 connectivity/source-fidelity assertions

## Source comparison

### TIDA-01389 Altium reference

Relevant crop from TI's official TIDRQE4 render of `TIDA-01389_Sch.SchDoc` in the TIDRQE8 Altium CAD/CAE archive:

![TIDA-01389 Altium reference showing the Inputs and Outputs and Hall Encoder sections](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/ba9aa4357c1efc8579d3e0422bfad5d49ea96afe/docs/images/position-feedback/tida-01389-altium-reference.png)

### Generated tscircuit schematic

![Generated PositionFeedback_DRV5013 schematic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/ba9aa4357c1efc8579d3e0422bfad5d49ea96afe/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/PositionFeedback_DRV5013.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)

## Reference-design provenance and scope

The Automotive Window Module page calls this function **Position Feedback — Hall Effect Sensors**, but its own Reference Design tab currently contains no design. This implementation therefore uses [TIDA-01389](https://www.ti.com/tool/TIDA-01389), selected from the closely related Motor Driver references. TI identifies TIDA-01389 for sunroof and window-lift applications, and its official implementation contains the two DRV5013-Q1 latching Hall sensors that encode motor position.

Sources used:

- [Automotive Window Module subsystem](https://www.ti.com/solution/automotive-window-module?variantid=34360&subsystemid=24693#subsystem-reference-design)
- [TIDA-01389 design page](https://www.ti.com/tool/TIDA-01389)
- TIDRQE8 official Altium CAD/CAE archive
- [TIDRQE4 official schematic PDF](https://www.ti.com/lit/df/tidrqe4/tidrqe4.pdf)
- TIDA-01389 BOM and [DRV5013-Q1 data sheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/drv5013-q1.pdf)

This PR is deliberately separate from #116. It reuses that PR's TIDA-01389 coordinate convention but does **not** duplicate the DRV8703-Q1 gate driver or H-bridge. The two branches extract complementary parts of the same TI design.

After merging current `main`, this PR also reuses the shared `DRV5013ADQDBZRQ1` chip definition introduced for `PositionFeedback_DRV5013_TIDA01389`; no duplicate chip or generic wrapper remains. That existing subcircuit is the Hall-only/PCB-aware Seat Position block. `PositionFeedback_DRV5013` remains the Window Module extraction because it additionally preserves the official J1/J2/J4/R9 connector section, dashed source boundaries, and the documented PR #116 schematic-coordinate transform.

## Coordinates and symbols

All source component and connector centers are derived with one documented transform:

```text
schX = (AltiumX - 185) * 0.018278145
schY = (AltiumY - 215) * 0.018278145
```

Child placement only subtracts the transformed section center; it does not manually re-layout components. The DRV5013 uses the native chip symbol and pin arrangement with DBZ pins validated as 1=VCC, 2=OUT (open drain), and 3=GND. J1/J2/J4 use native female pin-header symbols; J4 uses the BOM's 3.81 mm pitch and source bottom-to-top pin order. No Altium artwork is embedded, and no passive or net-label component uses a custom schematic size.

The source power label `+V_BAT` is represented by the repository-safe `V_BAT` net name because tscircuit selectors reject `+`/`-` characters in net names. Its source location, J4 pin assignment, and electrical connectivity are preserved.

## Routing note

The implementation uses ordinary trace declarations and the native schematic autorouter. U5/U6 pin 3, C13/C14 pin 2, J2 pin 1, and J4 pin 1 connect directly to `net.GND`; there are no explicit `<netlabel>` components for these connections. The focused snapshot renders the four Hall terminations as four native GND symbols, matching the TIDA-01389 reference.

The connector renderer places one generated GND symbol on the right of J2. Because J2 and J4 share one GND net and are close together, the current solver also renders a physical J4-to-J2 route; connectivity is correct, and the awkward route is left visible rather than hidden by a custom symbol or fake schematic line.

V_BAT alone uses trace-owned `schDisplayLabel` text for the source's inline label. R14/R15 retain repository-default passive dimensions and use the source `ORIENTATION=1` pin direction. Tests assert both complete output paths, the VCC rail, all six GND source traces, five generated native GND symbols, and J4's V_BAT connection.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- focused Position Feedback suite: 6 tests and 91 assertions
- focused subcircuit snapshot update and visual comparison against the reference
- `bun run build` — exit 0, 198 circuits generated (repository-wide offline supplier/KiCad/legacy warnings remain)
- local SVG inspection of the focused Position Feedback schematic

title: feat: add TMP390-Q1 motor thermal protection
description: Add a datasheet-derived implementation of the TMP390-Q1 motor thermal protection circuit, including new chip exports, schematic design, and validation tests.
body:
## Source classification

This is a **datasheet-derived implementation**, not an exact Automotive Window Module reference design.

## Reference and generated schematic

**Reference - TI TMP390-Q1 datasheet Figure 7-1**  
This is the TI product-page/datasheet image supplied as the visual reference; it is not Altium-derived.

![TI TMP390-Q1 Figure 7-1 reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/b220ba553f88553579e0f52f428bace5fb9f5d99/docs/images/motor-thermal-protection-tmp390-reference.png)

**Generated native tscircuit schematic snapshot (SVG)**

![Generated MotorThermalProtection_TMP390 schematic](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/ti/b220ba553f88553579e0f52f428bace5fb9f5d99/lib/subcircuits/__snapshots__/MotorThermalProtection_TMP390.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)

The TI Window Module “Motor thermal protection” subsystem recommends TMP390-Q1 but currently has no attached reference design or downloadable schematic/CAD. A search of official TI automotive body-motor/window/door/roof/seat/H-bridge reference designs did not locate a TMP390-Q1 design with downloadable CAD. The implementation therefore uses the official [TMP390-Q1 datasheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tmp390-q1.pdf):

- Figure 7-1 for topology and relative placement, following the supplied TI image
- Figure 8-3 and Tables 7-1/7-2 for the fixed example values and trip/reset behavior
- Figures 5-1 and 12-2 for pin mapping and the six-pad DRL land pattern

This complements the motor-driver context in #116 without claiming to reproduce a nonexistent Window Module reference schematic.

## What changed

- Added verified `TMP390AQDRLRQ1` and `TMP390Q1` chip exports with exact pins 1–6 and the datasheet DRL footprint.
- Added native-TSX `MotorThermalProtection_TMP390` with:
  - RSETA = 78.7 kΩ: +90 °C hot trip
  - RSETB = 215 kΩ: −25 °C cold trip, 10 °C hysteresis
  - +80 °C OUTA reset and −15 °C OUTB reset
  - two 10 kΩ open-drain output pull-ups
  - 0.1 µF VDD bypass
  - `VDD`, `VDDIO`, `GND`, `OUTA`, and `OUTB` ports
- Used native components, native schematic autorouting, native inline output labels, and small filled arrowheads at the right-side OUTA/OUTB endpoints. The arrowheads are graphics only; the electrical lines remain native traces. No image is embedded in the circuit.
- Updated the project-local `tscircuit` runtime to `^0.0.2448`, replaced manually positioned net labels with native trace-to-net connections, and restored native U1 symbol sizing.
- Added exports, source-scope documentation, schematic snapshot, exact-value/pin/footprint tests, and interface-net connectivity tests.

The TMP390-Q1 senses its own package temperature, so the source has no external sensor input. The source image also contains no connector or passive part/footprint selections; this implementation exposes native subcircuit ports and intentionally does not invent those physical details.

## Coordinate transform

The supplied Figure 7-1 capture is 1084 × 602 px. With the TMP39x block center `(573, 389)` as the source origin:

```text
schX = (sourcePixelX - 573) * 0.010 mm
schY = (389 - sourcePixelY) * 0.010 mm
```

Source centers: C1 `(154,376)`, R1 `(274,456)`, R2 `(321,475)`, R3 `(791,290)`, R4 `(859,290)`, VDD `(573,197)`, VDDIO `(824,198)`, GND `(575,549)`, OUTA `(1000,351)`, OUTB `(1000,427)`. Refdes are implementation-defined because Figure 7-1 has functional labels but no component designators.

Native-symbol normalization places both threshold-resistor lower pins on a shared straight ground baseline at `schY = -1.6 mm`; R2 is shifted `0.42 mm` right so the native value labels remain legible. The right-side pull-ups, VDDIO, and output endpoints are shifted `0.72-0.93 mm` right to clear U1's native part-number text. U1 uses tscircuit's default native chip box and pin spacing, and OUTA/OUTB are aligned to its output pins and terminate in right-pointing arrows. This deliberately normalizes symbol geometry instead of claiming exact source coordinates for details the source does not define.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run snapshot:update -- lib/subcircuits/MotorThermalProtection_TMP390.circuit.tsx --schematic-only` — focused SVG snapshot is up to date
- `bun test` — 9 passed, 91 assertions
- `bun run build` — 159 circuits passed, exit 0 (existing repository-wide supplier/footprint/routing diagnostics remain)
- `bun run dev` — visually inspected the final schematic; no floating traces or obstacle violations observed

title: feat(block-ui): add Rearview Mirror Module
description: Add Rearview Mirror Module as an editable System Block UI example, including semantic adapters for application blocks, resolving internal power and data links, and fixing selector generation for nested components.
body:
## Summary

- register the Rearview Mirror Module as an editable System Block UI example
- add reviewed semantic adapters for all seven application blocks
- resolve 16 internal power and data links covering 3.3 V, protected vehicle power, CAN controller, I2C, sensor inputs, driver controls and power monitoring
- support curated subcircuits located under `lib/thirdparty-subcircuits`
- fix generated selectors for components nested inside subcircuits
- preserve per-block schematic offsets so wide detail sheets fit PDF borders
- add focused coverage for catalog paths, exact selectors, generated TSX and the system diagram

## Why these adapter changes are needed

The Rearview example already existed as circuit TSX, but the System Block UI only had a TCAN1042 adapter and basic MSPM0G3507 power metadata. The remaining blocks and MCU interfaces therefore could not be composed or resolved by the UI.

The TCAN1042 power selectors were updated to preserve the subcircuit boundary shown by the existing design:

- 5 V enters through `R21.pin1`; `R21.pin2` feeds `U6.VCC` and its decoupling capacitor
- 3.3 V enters through `R22.pin1`; `R22.pin2` feeds `U6.VIO` and its decoupling capacitor

Connecting generated power directly to `U6.VCC` or `U6.VIO` would place it on the device side of those 0 ohm series resistors. The explicit `requiredSignals` and `signals` entries are System Block UI metadata only: they require both positive and ground and identify their direction and selectors; they do not modify the underlying circuit.

The CAN bus selectors use `R23.pin1` and `R24.pin2` to match the existing Rearview example trace endpoints. These are electrically the same `CANH` and `CANL` nets as `L7.pin3` and `L7.pin2`, respectively.

Rail-specific power protocols distinguish the 3.3 V logic rail from protected vehicle power when the same two blocks require both supplies. External vehicle battery, regulated 5 V CAN power and the vehicle CAN bus remain external interfaces, consistent with `examples/RearviewMirrorModule.circuit.tsx`.

## Nested selector render fix

The OPT3001 block contains `U4` and `U5` inside nested `U4Sensor` and `U5Sensor` subcircuits. Generated selectors incorrectly inserted a child combinator before the nested path, producing `.light_sensor > .U4Sensor .U4 > .SCL`. tscircuit expects the working descendant form `.light_sensor .U4Sensor .U4 > .SCL`. The generator now preserves that nested selector form while retaining direct-child selectors for ordinary blocks.

## Power sheet PDF fit

Generated block instances previously had no way to preserve a detail-sheet schematic offset. The Power Supply was therefore centered at `schX={0}`, which placed its right-side 3.3 V output and `C_LDO_OUT` beyond the title-block border in the downloaded PDF. `BlockInstance` now supports validated `schX` and `schY` offsets, the generator emits them, and the Rearview Power Supply uses the same `schX={-3.6}` placement as the existing hand-authored example. A real worker evaluation confirms `V3P3` is inside the rendered sheet.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck` in `system-block-ui`
- `bun test` in `system-block-ui` — 59 passing

title: feat: add conflict-directed HighDensitySolverB02
description: Summary add the new numbered HighDensitySolverB02 compose B01 as a bounded partial-route seed plus conflict-directed repair support planar and cross-layer repair while preserving exact pair, endpoint, root, region, transition, and via identity publish output only after strict tracevia clearance validation export defaultB02Params, add B02 to the Cosmos debugger, and document the API fail loudly for unsupported obstacles and invalid child-solver setup  Why Bugreport 101 exposed individual high-density nodes that dominate the CM5 route time. The dominant 11-pair node previously consumed about 51.6 seconds in the portfolio. B02 solves the exact captured node in roughly 0.280.31 seconds in focused local runs, while returning all 11 routes with zero geometry violations at 0.15 mm trace width plus 0.10 mm clearance. ## Summary

- publish output only after strict trace/via clearance validation

Bugreport 101 exposed individual high-density nodes that dominate the CM5 route time. The dominant 11-pair node previously consumed about 51.6 seconds in the portfolio. - terminal-spacing feasibility rejection

title: fix : resolve component-owned schematic parameter references
description: Fixes rendering issue where component-owned parameter references are displayed as literal text instead of their resolved values in schematic SVGs.
body:
## Problem

The schematic SVG renderer leaves component-owned parameter references such as `=Value` as literal text instead of resolving them against the owning component.

For example, a capacitor containing a visible `Comment = =Value` and a hidden `Value = 100nF` is rendered as `=Value` rather than `100nF`.

## Fix

- locate the component that owns the rendered schematic parameter record
- add that component’s built-in fields and parameter records to the resolution context
- resolve parameter names case-insensitively
- retain document-level and project-level parameter resolution
- preserve unresolved or cyclic references as their original display text

## Real-board verification

The regression uses the unmodified, GPL-3.0-licensed [`yasir-shahzad/STM32-ST-Link-V2.0-Programmer`](https://github.com/yasir-shahzad/STM32-ST-Link-V2.0-Programmer) schematic, pinned to commit `3284ac4fbd9a3f8471844db3c2b368fff2c33ca9` with SHA-256 verification.

The original board naturally contains:

- an 8 MHz crystal labeled `8MHz(12pF)`
- ten visible capacitor comments containing `=Value`
- matching hidden component `Value` parameters

After the fix, the SVG contains no literal `=Value` labels. They resolve to:

- six `100nF`
- two `20pF`
- two `47pF`

The test does not modify the source schematic.

## Test plan

- `bun test tests/svg/schematic-component-value-reference.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/svg/schematic-parameter-reference.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/svg`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`

Reproduction: #79

title: Add real Altium board regression tests
description: Adds real open-source Altium corpus for PCB and schematic regression tests, including fixes for component value parsing and improved validation checks.
body:
## What changed

Adds the same real open-source Altium corpus used by `circuit-json-to-altium`:

- PCB snapshots: NodeMCU ESP-12, EBAZ4205, HERON Payload SSM, SimpleFOC Mini, and SimpleFOC Shield V3.
- Schematic snapshots: NodeMCU ESP-12, HERON PAY-SSM, HERON Systems PCB, SimpleFOC Mini, and SimpleFOC Shield V3.

Each design has one test file and one side-by-side SVG snapshot: native AltiumTS rendering on the left and imported Circuit JSON rendering on the right. The snapshots are produced directly by `bun-match-svg`; the SVG/XML is not rewritten or annotated.

The new sources are checksum-pinned to upstream commits and retain their MIT or CERN-OHL-P source attribution in the reference manifest.

## Converter fix found by the corpus

SimpleFOC Shield uses `L1` for an `L78M08CDT-TR` regulator. The converter treated every `L` designator as an inductor and emitted `NaN` for its inductance, which failed the Circuit JSON schema.

Passive and crystal values are now classified as specialized Circuit JSON components only when their displayed value parses to a finite value in the expected SI unit. Otherwise the component remains a valid generic chip and keeps its original display text.

## Code quality

- Shared PCB and schematic comparison helpers use named parameter objects.
- Shared validity checks verify Circuit JSON schemas, required geometry, detached ports, and invalid SVG output.
- The existing three-argument SVG stack helper was converted to a named-parameter API to follow the tscircuit handbook.

title: Fix custom schematic symbol text fidelity
description: Fixes rendering issues with custom schematic symbols by treating schematic text as a first-class primitive, ensuring proper color parsing and font usage, and preventing duplicate outputs.
body:
## Summary

- treats `schematic_text` owned by a `schematic_symbol_id` as a first-class custom-symbol primitive
- merges component-owned and symbol-owned primitives without duplicate output, and keeps symbol text out of sheet/net-label and component designator matching
- hides converter-inferred designator and pin text when custom primitives already define the symbol presentation
- parses CSS color syntax through exactly pinned `color-string@2.1.4`, uses the shared Altium schematic graphic color for missing primitive colors, and uses Arial for source schematic text

## Root cause

The converter selected component-owned primitives or symbol-owned primitives, but not both. The Logic/Control triangle contains both ownership forms, so its symbol-owned `LVC1G34` text was discarded. The later fallback then invented a designator and pin labels. Separately, valid `rgb()` / `rgba()` colors fell through the hex-only parser, and schematic text was assigned Times New Roman despite the source renderer using sans-serif.

## Visual diff

The Consumer Wireless Module Logic/Control snapshot now preserves `LVC1G34`, removes the invented component/pin presentation, renders the custom symbol in its source red, and uses a matching sans-serif font.

title: Preserve PCB keepout outlines
description: Preserves PCB keepout outlines by reading Track and Arc keepouts as outlines, parsing them through the official Circuit JSON schema, and writing them as native Altium Track records without altering existing filled keepouts.
body:
## Why

Several real Altium boards define keepouts as stroked Track and Arc outlines. The round-trip importer only understood filled rectangular and circular keepouts, so it dropped shaped board-edge boundaries and incorrectly turned circular Arc keepouts into filled regions.

These are outlines rather than polygons: many are open, and the area inside them is not itself a filled keepout.

## What changed

- Read Track and Arc keepouts as `pcb_keepout` outlines with their points, layer, and stroke width
- Parse outlines through the official Circuit JSON keepout schema
- Write keepout outlines as native Altium Track records with `KEEPOUT=TRUE`
- Keep filled Region/Fill keepouts on the existing rectangle/circle handling
- Add one focused native-track SVG snapshot test
- Update the four real-board snapshots whose keepout outlines are now preserved

This retains the actual thin keepout geometry. It does not infer a filled polygon, replace it with a drawing annotation, or alter the SVG.

## Dependencies

- `circuit-json@^0.0.480`, containing the merged keepout-outline schema from https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/736
- `altiumts#f95e9b1a859bc433444c25ec3fd283718c032408`, the `main` commit containing merged Track keepout support from https://github.com/tscircuit/altiumts/pull/82

## Visual proof

- NodeMCU ESP-12: notched perimeter keepout restored
- EBAZ4205: rounded perimeter and four outlined circular keepouts restored
- SimpleFOC Mini: rounded keepout boundary restored
- SimpleFOC Shield V3: shaped perimeter keepout restored
- HERON fill keepouts remain unchanged

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test --max-concurrency=1` — 52 pass across 51 files
- Inspected the focused and all four changed real-board SVG snapshots

title: Fix FabricationNoteText layer handling
description: Fixes incorrect handling of FabricationNoteText layer, ensuring notes are placed on the correct side of the PCB based on their specified layer and component placement.
body:
## Why

FabricationNoteText currently writes every pcb_fabrication_note_text element to the top layer, even when the JSX specifies layer="bottom" or the note belongs to a component whose footprint is flipped to the bottom side.

That produces incorrect Circuit JSON for bottom-side fabrication notes. Downstream renderers and fabrication tooling receive the note on the wrong side, and importing existing Circuit JSON also loses the original fabrication-note text layer.

## What changed

- Resolve FabricationNoteText from its layer prop instead of hard-coding top.
- Apply the existing PCB primitive layer-flip helper so notes follow bottom-side component and footprint placement consistently with other fabrication-note primitives.
- Validate that the resolved fabrication-note text layer is top or bottom.
- Preserve pcb_fabrication_note_text.layer when rebuilding components from Circuit JSON.
- Add a visual regression test covering both an explicit bottom layer and a note inherited through a bottom-layer component container.

## Testing

- bun test tests/components/primitive-components/fabrication-note-text-layer.test.tsx tests/components/primitive-components/fabrication-note-text-rotation.test.tsx tests/components/normal-components/fabrication-notes.test.tsx
- bunx tsc --noEmit

title: Fix fabrication note path layers on bottom components
description: Fixes the layer assignment for FabricationNotePath to correctly reflect the components layer, preventing incorrect rendering and export of paths on the wrong side of the PCB.
body:
## Summary

- Resolve fabrication note path layers relative to their primitive container, matching silkscreen paths and the other fabrication-note primitives.
- Correct the invalid-layer error so it names FabricationNotePath.
- Add a regression test and bottom-layer PCB snapshot.

## Why this change is needed

When a footprint is placed on a bottom-layer component, its primitives are defined in footprint-local layer space. Core already mirrors the path geometry through the component transform, but FabricationNotePath previously assigned its layer directly from props.layer ?? "top". As a result, a path without an explicit layer produced mirrored bottom-side geometry while its Circuit JSON still declared layer: "top". Viewers and fabrication exporters could therefore display or export the path on the wrong side.

SilkscreenPath and sibling fabrication-note primitives resolve their layer with _getPcbPrimitiveFlippedHelpers(). This change applies the same resolution to FabricationNotePath, so the default footprint-local top layer becomes bottom when the containing component is flipped.

## Validation

title: feat: compact residual via lines symmetrically
description: Arranges residual ViaLine groups in a compact symmetric V instead of a monotonic staircase, improving routing efficiency and reducing solve time for specific layouts.
body:
## Summary

- arrange residual ViaLine groups in a compact symmetric V instead of a monotonic staircase
- bend upper and lower groups away from the horizontal midpoint and mirror upper slot order to avoid trace crossings
- keep the placement policy owned by CompleteTopLayerRoutesSolver
- cap best-effort power-conflict top reroutes at 100k events to avoid exhaustive futile trials

## Performance

Fixed-layer SoC fixture, CLI solve time:

- parent baseline: 39.3s
- V layout before performance bound: 93.3s
- V layout with bounded fallback: 33.1s

The regression was isolated to resolvePowerSignalConflicts: the V layout increased affected signals from 7 to 10 and expanded a failing selective top-route trial from about 52k to 414k events. The primary signal router is unchanged by the new bound; only the best-effort power-conflict fallback is capped, and invalid trials cannot replace the validated baseline.

## Validation
